sentences.zh: 王汝訓余懋學張養蒙孟一脈何士晉

translations.literal: Wang Ruxun, Yu Maoxue, Zhang Yangmeng, Meng Yimai, He Shijin
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruxun, Yu Maoxue, Zhang Yangmeng, Meng Yimai, and He Shijin

sentences.zh: 〈（陸大受張庭李俸）〉

translations.literal: (Lu Dashou, Zhang Ting, Li Feng)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Lu Dashou, Zhang Ting, and Li Feng)]〉

sentences.zh: 王德完蔣允儀鄒維璉

translations.literal: Wang Dewan, Jiang Yunyi, Zou Weilian
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dewan, Jiang Yunyi, and Zou Weilian

sentences.zh: 〈（吳羽文）〉

translations.literal: (Wu Yuwen)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Wu Yuwen)]〉

sentences.zh: 王汝訓，字古師，聊城人。

translations.literal: Wang Ruxun, style name Gushi, was a native of Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruxun, whose style was Gushi, came from Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 除元城知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yuancheng County.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，入為刑部主事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, he entered the capital as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he was called to the capital and made a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 改兵部，累遷光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of War and was promoted in stages to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: After a transfer to the Ministry of War, he rose by stages to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 吏科都給事中海寧陳與郊者，大學士王錫爵門生，又附申時行，恣甚。

translations.literal: Chen Yujiao of Haining, supervising secretary of the Personnel Section of the Censorate, was a disciple of Grand Secretary Wang Xijue and also attached himself to Shen Shixing; he was extremely overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yujiao of Haining, chief supervising secretary in the personnel section of the censorate, was a protégé of Grand Secretary Wang Xijue and also curried favor with Shen Shixing; he behaved with great arrogance.

sentences.zh: 汝訓抗疏數其罪，言：「與郊今日薦巡撫，明日薦監司。

translations.literal: Ruxun submitted a forthright memorial enumerating his crimes, saying: Yujiao today recommends a grand coordinator, tomorrow a surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun submitted a bold memorial listing Chen's offenses, writing: "Today Yujiao recommends a grand coordinator; tomorrow he recommends a surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 每疏一出，受賄狼籍。

translations.literal: Whenever a memorial goes out, bribes are received in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: Every time a memorial goes out, bribes pour in unchecked.

sentences.zh: 部曹吳正誌一發其奸，身投荒僥。

translations.literal: A ministry clerk, Wu Zhengzhi, once exposed his villainy and cast himself into the wilderness in peril.
translations.idiomatic: A ministry clerk named Wu Zhengzhi once exposed his corruption and fled into exile at the risk of his life.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書楊巍亦嘗語侍郎趙煥，謂為小人。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Yang Wei also once told Vice Minister Zhao Huan that he was a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Yang Wei had also told Vice Minister Zhao Huan that Chen was a base man.

sentences.zh: 乞速罷譴。

translations.literal: I beg that he be swiftly dismissed and punished.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be dismissed and punished without delay.

sentences.zh: 且科道以言為職，乃默默者顯，諤諤者絀。

translations.literal: Moreover, the censorate and supervising secretaries take speech as their duty, yet the silent are made prominent and the outspoken are disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, censors and supervising secretaries are charged with speaking out, yet the silent are rewarded with prominence while the outspoken are disgraced.

sentences.zh: 直犯乘輿，屢荷優容。

translations.literal: Those who directly offend the imperial carriage have repeatedly received gracious forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Those who directly reprove the throne have again and again been treated with leniency.

sentences.zh: 稍涉當途，旋遭擯斥。

translations.literal: Those who touch even slightly on those in power are at once cast out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who touch even slightly on men in power are at once cast aside.

sentences.zh: 言官不難於批鱗，而難於借劍，此何為也？

translations.literal: It is not hard for remonstrating officials to touch the dragon's scales, but hard to borrow the sword—what is the reason for this?
translations.idiomatic: It is not hard for remonstrating officials to touch the dragon's scales, but hard to borrow the sword—what does this mean?

sentences.zh: 天下惟公足以服人。

translations.literal: Under Heaven only fairness is sufficient to win people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Heaven, only fairness can win men's assent.

sentences.zh: 今言者不論是非，被言者不論邪正，模棱兩可，曲事調停，而曰務存大體。

translations.literal: Now accusers are not judged on right and wrong, the accused are not judged on wickedness or uprightness; things are left equivocal and bent to compromise, yet it is called preserving the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Today accusers are not judged on the merits, and the accused are not judged on whether they are wicked or upright; everything is left equivocal and bent toward compromise, all in the name of preserving the larger pattern.

sentences.zh: 是懲議論之紛紜，而反致政體之決裂也。

translations.literal: This is to punish the confusion of debate and instead bring about the rupture of the polity.
translations.idiomatic: This punishes the confusion of debate only to rupture the body politic itself.

sentences.zh: 乞特敕吏部，自後遷轉科道，毋惡異喜同，毋好諛醜正。」

translations.literal: I beg a special edict to the Ministry of Personnel that henceforth in transferring censors and supervising secretaries they must not hate difference and love sameness, nor favor flattery and abhor uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty specially instruct the Ministry of Personnel that henceforth, in promoting censors and supervising secretaries, they must not hate difference and love sameness, nor favor flattery and abhor integrity.

sentences.zh: 是時，巍以政府故，方厚與郊。

translations.literal: At that time, because of the government, Wei was then treating Yujiao generously.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Wei, owing to his ties to the government, was treating Yujiao with great favor.

sentences.zh: 聞汝訓言引己且刺之，大恚，言：「臣未嘗詆與郊。

translations.literal: Hearing Ruxun's words implicate himself and moreover stab at him, he was greatly enraged and said: Your subject has never slandered Yujiao.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Ruxun's words implicated him and attacked him personally, he was furious and said, "Your subject has never slandered Yujiao.

sentences.zh: 汝訓以寺臣攻言路，正決裂政體之大者。」

translations.literal: Ruxun, as a court-of-rites official, attacks the remonstrance route—this is precisely the great matter that ruptures the polity.
translations.idiomatic: For Ruxun, a court-of-rites official, to attack the remonstrance route is precisely the sort of thing that ruptures the polity.

sentences.zh: 乃調汝訓南京。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ruxun was transferred to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun was thereupon transferred to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 頃之，御史王明復劾與郊，並及巍，詔奪明俸，擢與郊太常少卿。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, censor Wang Ming again impeached Yujiao and implicated Wei as well; an edict stripped Ming of his salary and promoted Yujiao to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the censor Wang Ming impeached Yujiao again and implicated Wei as well; an edict stripped Wang of his salary while Yujiao was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 都人為之語曰：「欲京堂，須彈章。」

translations.literal: The people of the capital made a saying of it: If you want a capital post, you need an impeachment memorial.
translations.idiomatic: People in the capital made up a saying: "If you want a capital post, you need an impeachment memorial.

sentences.zh: 與郊尋以憂去。

translations.literal: Yujiao soon left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yujiao soon left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 後御史張應揚追劾其交通文選郎劉希孟，考選納賄，並免官。

translations.literal: Later censor Zhang Yingyang pursued impeachment of his dealings with Selection Secretary Liu Ximeng and taking bribes in examinations and appointments; both were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Later the censor Zhang Yingyang pursued charges that he had colluded with Selection Secretary Liu Ximeng and taken bribes in examinations and appointments; both men were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其子殺人論死，與郊悒悒卒。

translations.literal: Before long his son was sentenced to death for murder, and Yujiao died in dejection.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his son was sentenced to death for murder, and Yujiao died in gloom and distress.

sentences.zh: 汝訓入為太常少卿。

translations.literal: Ruxun entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun was recalled to the capital as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 孟秋饗廟，帝不親行。

translations.literal: At the mid-autumn temple feast, the emperor did not go in person.
translations.idiomatic: At the mid-autumn temple sacrifice the emperor did not attend in person.

sentences.zh: 汝訓極諫。

translations.literal: Ruxun remonstrated to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun remonstrated forcefully.

sentences.zh: 帝慍甚，以其言直，不罪也。

translations.literal: The emperor was very angry, but because his words were straightforward, he did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered, yet because his words were forthright he did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 尋進太仆卿，調光祿。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and transferred to the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and then transferred to the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 汝訓先為少卿，寺中歲費二十萬，至是濫增四萬有奇。

translations.literal: Ruxun had earlier been vice minister; the court's annual expenditure was two hundred thousand, and by this time it had wantonly increased by more than forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun had earlier served as vice minister, when the court's annual expenditure was two hundred thousand; by now it had wantonly risen by more than forty thousand.

sentences.zh: 汝訓據《會典》，請盡裁內府冗食，不許。

translations.literal: Ruxun, citing the 《Collected Statutes》, requested that all redundant eaters in the inner palace be cut; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun, citing the 《Collected Statutes》, asked to cut all redundant retainers in the inner palace, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，改左僉都御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was changed to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of the reign he was made left assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 旋進右副都御史，巡撫浙江。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 汝訓性清介，方嚴疾惡。

translations.literal: Ruxun's nature was pure and upright; he was square and stern and hated evil.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun was pure and upright by nature, stern and unyielding, and hated wickedness.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史南昌彭應參亦雅以強直名，相與力鋤豪右。

translations.literal: Touring censor Peng Yingcan of Nanchang was also known for his forceful uprightness; together they vigorously uprooted powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor Peng Yingcan of Nanchang was also famed for his forceful integrity; together they worked hard to uproot powerful local families.

sentences.zh: 烏程故尚書董份、祭酒範應期裏居不法，汝訓將繩之。

translations.literal: Former Minister Dong Fen and Libationer Fan Yingqi of Wucheng, living in retirement at home, acted unlawfully; Ruxun was about to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The former minister Dong Fen and the former libationer Fan Yingqi of Wucheng, living in retirement at home, had broken the law; Ruxun was about to bring them to account.

sentences.zh: 適應參行部至，應期怨家千人遮道陳牒。

translations.literal: Just as Yingcan arrived on his circuit, a thousand of Yingqi's enemies blocked the road presenting petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Yingcan arrived on his inspection tour, a thousand of Yingqi's enemies blocked the road to present petitions.

sentences.zh: 應參持之急，檄烏程知縣張應望按之。

translations.literal: Yingcan pressed the case urgently and ordered Wucheng magistrate Zhang Yingwang to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Yingcan pressed the case hard and ordered Zhang Yingwang, magistrate of Wucheng, to investigate.

sentences.zh: 應期自縊死，其妻吳氏詣闕訴冤。

translations.literal: Yingqi hanged himself; his wife, the Lady Wu, went to the palace gate to plead her wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqi hanged himself, and his wife Lady Wu went to the palace gate to plead that an injustice had been done.

sentences.zh: 帝命逮應參、應望詔獄，革汝訓職，詰吏部都察院任用非人。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yingcan and Yingwang seized and sent to the imperial prison, stripped Ruxun of his post, and rebuked the Ministry of Personnel and the Censorate for employing unfit men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yingcan and Yingwang arrested and sent to the imperial prison, stripped Ruxun of his office, and rebuked the Ministry of Personnel and the Censorate for appointing unfit men.

sentences.zh: 尚書孫丕揚、都御史衷貞吉等引罪，且論救。

translations.literal: Minister Sun Piyang, Censor-in-Chief Yuan Zhenji, and others took blame upon themselves and also pleaded for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Sun Piyang, Censor-in-Chief Yuan Zhenji, and others accepted blame and also pleaded for the men's release.

sentences.zh: 帝意未釋，謫救應參者給事中喬胤等於外。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was not yet eased; he demoted the supervising secretaries Qiao Yin and others, who had pleaded for Yingcan, to posts outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger had not yet subsided; he demoted the supervising secretaries Qiao Yin and others, who had pleaded for Yingcan, to posts outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 言官訟汝訓、應參，亦及胤，帝愈怒。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials sued on behalf of Ruxun and Yingcan and also implicated Yin; the emperor grew angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials petitioned on behalf of Ruxun and Yingcan and also implicated Yin; the emperor grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 疏入，輒重胤譴，至除名，而謫應望戍煙瘴，應參為民。

translations.literal: Whenever a memorial entered, Yin was punished more heavily, until he was removed from the rolls; Yingwang was demoted to guard duty in the miasmal south, and Yingcan was made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Each new memorial only deepened Yin's punishment, until he was struck from the rolls; Yingwang was banished to guard duty in the miasmal south, and Yingcan was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 汝訓家居十五年，起南京刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Ruxun lived at home for fifteen years, then was raised as Right Vice Minister of Punishments in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun lived in retirement for fifteen years, then was recalled as right vice minister of punishments in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 召改工部，署部事。

translations.literal: He was summoned and transferred to the Ministry of Works, acting as head of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the Ministry of Works and placed in charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，礦稅興，以助大工為名。

translations.literal: At first the mining tax was instituted in the name of aiding great construction projects.
translations.idiomatic: When the mining tax was first imposed, it was said to be for major construction projects.

sentences.zh: 後悉輸內帑，不以供營繕。

translations.literal: Later it was all paid into the inner treasury and was not used to supply repairs and construction.
translations.idiomatic: Later it all went into the inner treasury and was no longer used for repairs or construction.

sentences.zh: 而四方采木之需多至千萬，費益不訾。

translations.literal: Yet the need for timber from all quarters often reached tens of millions, and expenses grew beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet demands for timber from all quarters often ran into the tens of millions, and costs grew beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 汝訓屢請發帑佐工，皆不報。

translations.literal: Ruxun repeatedly requested that treasury funds be released to aid the works; there was never any reply.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun repeatedly asked that treasury funds be released to support the works, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 在部歲餘，力清夙弊。

translations.literal: During more than a year in the ministry, he strove to clear long-standing abuses.
translations.idiomatic: During more than a year at the ministry he worked hard to clear long-standing abuses.

sentences.zh: 中官請乞，輒執奏不予，節冗費數萬。

translations.literal: Whenever eunuchs made requests, he would hold firm in memorial and refuse; he cut redundant expenses by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever eunuchs made requests he memorialized the throne and refused them, saving tens of thousands in redundant expenses.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書，謚恭介。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Gongjie.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made minister of works and given the posthumous title Gongjie, "Respectful and Upright."

sentences.zh: 余懋學，字行之，婺源人。

translations.literal: Yu Maoxue, style name Xingzhi, was a native of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Maoxue, whose style was Xingzhi, came from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 授撫州推官，擢南京戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed reviewing official of Fuzhou and was promoted to supervising secretary of the Revenue Section in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed reviewing official in Fuzhou and was then promoted to supervising secretary in the revenue section of the Nanjing censorate.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，張居正當國，進《白燕白蓮頌》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, Zhang Juzheng held power and presented the 《Odes to the White Swallow and White Lotus》.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign, with Zhang Juzheng in power, he presented the 《Odes to the White Swallow and White Lotus》.

sentences.zh: 懋學以帝方憂旱，下詔罪己，與百官圖修禳。

translations.literal: Maoxue, because the emperor was then worried about drought, had issued an edict blaming himself and was with the hundred officials planning prayers for rain.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxue noted that the emperor was then troubled by drought, had issued a self-reproach edict, and was working with his officials on prayers for rain.

sentences.zh: 而居正顧獻瑞，非大臣誼，抗疏論之。

translations.literal: Yet Juzheng instead offered auspicious omens—this was not the duty of a great minister; he submitted a forthright memorial discussing it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Juzheng instead offered auspicious omens, which was unbecoming in a great minister; Maoxue submitted a bold memorial criticizing him.

sentences.zh: 已，論南京守備太監申信不法，帝為罷信。

translations.literal: Later he discussed the unlawful conduct of Nanjing garrison eunuch Shen Xin; the emperor dismissed Xin on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Later he denounced the unlawful conduct of the Nanjing garrison eunuch Shen Xin, and the emperor dismissed Xin on his account.

sentences.zh: 久之，陳崇惇大、親謇諤、慎名器、戒紛更、防佞諛五事。

translations.literal: After a long time he set forth five matters: revering great virtue, cherishing outspoken integrity, being careful with titles and offices, guarding against frequent changes, and guarding against flattery.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he set forth five matters: revering great virtue, cherishing outspoken integrity, being careful with titles and offices, guarding against frequent policy changes, and guarding against flattery.

sentences.zh: 時居正方務綜核，而懋學疏與之忤，斥為民，永不敘錄。

translations.literal: At that time Juzheng was just then bent on comprehensive verification, and Maoxue's memorial ran counter to him; he was expelled as a commoner and never again recorded for office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Juzheng was bent on tightening administrative control, and Maoxue's memorial ran counter to him; he was reduced to commoner status and never again considered for office.

sentences.zh: 居正死，起懋學故官，奏奪成國公朱希忠王爵，請召還光祿少卿嶽相、給事中魏時亮等十八人。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, Maoxue was raised to his former office; he memorialized to strip Duke of Chengguo Zhu Xizhong of his princely rank and requested the recall of Court of Imperial Entertainments Vice Minister Yue Xiang, supervising secretary Wei Shiliang, and eighteen others.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death Maoxue was restored to his former office; he memorialized to strip Zhu Xizhong, Duke of Chengguo, of his princely rank and asked that Yue Xiang, Wei Shiliang, and eighteen others be recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 帝俱報可。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these requests.

sentences.zh: 尋擢南京尚寶卿。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to Court of Imperial Seals Minister in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to minister of the Court of Imperial Seals in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十三年，御史李植、江東之等以言事忤執政。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, censors Li Zhi, Jiang Dongzhi, and others offended the chief ministers by their remonstrances.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the censors Li Zhi, Jiang Dongzhi, and others offended the chief ministers by their remonstrances.

sentences.zh: 同官蔡系周、孫愈賢希執政指，紛然攻訐，懋學上言：

translations.literal: Colleagues Cai Xizhou and Sun Yuxian, hoping for the chief ministers' direction, attacked them in a clamor; Maoxue submitted a statement:
translations.idiomatic: Their colleagues Cai Xizhou and Sun Yuxian, eager to follow the chief ministers' lead, attacked them in a clamor; Maoxue submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 諸臣之不能容植等，一則以科場不能無私，而惡植等之訐發；

translations.literal: The reason the various ministers cannot tolerate Zhi and the others: first, because the examination fields cannot be without private interest, they hate Zhi and the others for exposing and denouncing;
translations.idiomatic: "The ministers cannot tolerate Zhi and the others for two reasons. First, because examination fields cannot be wholly free of private interest, they hate Zhi and the others for exposing wrongdoing;

sentences.zh: 一則以往者常保留居正，而忌吳中行、沈思孝等之召用。

translations.literal: second, because in former times they often shielded Juzheng, they are jealous of the recall of Wu Zhongxing, Shen Sixiao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: second, because they once shielded Juzheng, they resent the recall of Wu Zhongxing, Shen Sixiao, and others.

sentences.zh: 二疑交於中，故百妒發於外也。

translations.literal: These two suspicions cross within, and therefore a hundred jealousies burst forth without.
translations.idiomatic: These two suspicions meet within the court, and so a hundred jealousies burst forth without."

sentences.zh: 夫威福自上，則主勢尊。

translations.literal: When authority and favor come from above, then the ruler's position is honored.
translations.idiomatic: When authority and favor come from above, the ruler's position is honored.

sentences.zh: 植等三臣，陛下所親擢者也，乃舉朝臣工百計排之；

translations.literal: The three ministers Zhi and the others were personally promoted by Your Majesty, yet the whole court of officials contrives by a hundred schemes to exclude them;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and two other ministers were personally promoted by Your Majesty, yet the whole court contrives by a hundred schemes to exclude them;

sentences.zh: 假令政府欲用一人，諸臣敢力挫之乎？

translations.literal: suppose the government wished to employ one man—would the various ministers dare to thwart him by force?
translations.idiomatic: yet if the government wished to employ one man, would the ministers dare to thwart him by force?

sentences.zh: 臣謹以臣工之十蠹為陛下言之。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully sets forth for Your Majesty the ten corruptions of the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully sets forth for Your Majesty the ten corruptions of the official class.

sentences.zh: 今執政大臣，一政之善，輒矜贊導之功，一事之失，輒諉挽回之難，是為誣上。

translations.literal: The chief ministers today: for one good policy they at once boast of the merit of guiding it; for one fault they at once blame the difficulty of remedying it—this is deceiving the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Today's chief ministers boast of their merit whenever a policy succeeds, yet blame the difficulty of remedying matters whenever something goes wrong—this is deceiving the ruler.

sentences.zh: 其蠹一。

translations.literal: This is corruption the first.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first corruption.

sentences.zh: 進用一人，執政則曰我所註意也，冢宰則曰我所推轂也，選郎則曰我所登用也。

translations.literal: When one man is advanced, the chief minister says I was the one who marked him; the minister of personnel says I was the one who pushed him forward; the selection secretary says I was the one who placed him.
translations.idiomatic: When a man is promoted, the chief minister says, "I marked him for attention"; the minister of personnel says, "I pushed him forward"; the selection secretary says, "I placed him in office."

sentences.zh: 受爵公朝，拜恩私室，是為招權。

translations.literal: They receive rank in the public court and pay homage to favor in private chambers—this is inviting power.
translations.idiomatic: They receive rank in the public court yet pay homage to favor in private chambers—this is inviting power.

sentences.zh: 其蠹二。

translations.literal: This is corruption the second.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second corruption.

sentences.zh: 陛下天縱聖明，猶虛懷納諫。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is heaven-endowed with sagely brilliance and still humbly accepts remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is heaven-endowed with sagely brilliance and still humbly accepts remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 乃二三大僚，稍有規正，輒奮袂而起，惡聲相加，是為諱疾。

translations.literal: Yet the two or three great ministers, whenever there is slight correction, at once fling up their sleeves and rise, adding harsh voices to one another—this is concealing sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two or three great ministers, whenever they are slightly corrected, at once fling up their sleeves and rise, heaping abuse on one another—this is concealing sickness.

sentences.zh: 其蠹三。

translations.literal: This is corruption the third.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third corruption.

sentences.zh: 中外臣工，率探政府意向，而不恤公論。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials within and without all probe the government's intent and do not care for public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Officials within and without the court all probe the government's intent and care nothing for public opinion.

sentences.zh: 論人則毀譽視其愛憎，行政則舉置徇其喜怒，是為承望。

translations.literal: In discussing men, praise and blame follow love and hate; in administering affairs, promotion and dismissal follow joy and anger—this is courting expectation.
translations.idiomatic: In judging men, praise and blame follow personal likes and dislikes; in administering affairs, promotion and dismissal follow the ruler's moods—this is courting expectation.

sentences.zh: 其蠹四。

translations.literal: This is corruption the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth corruption.

sentences.zh: 君子立身，和而不同。

translations.literal: The gentleman in establishing himself is harmonious but not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman stands firm in harmony without sameness.

sentences.zh: 今當路意有所主，則群相附和，敢於抗天子，而難於違大臣，是為雷同。

translations.literal: Now when those on the road of power have a fixed intent, the crowd echoes one another, daring to resist the Son of Heaven yet finding it hard to go against great ministers—this is sameness in echo.
translations.idiomatic: Today when men in power have a fixed intent, the crowd echoes them, daring to resist the Son of Heaven yet finding it hard to defy great ministers—this is sameness in echo.

sentences.zh: 其蠹五。

translations.literal: This is corruption the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth corruption.

sentences.zh: 我國家諫無專官，今他曹稍有建白，不曰出位，則曰沽名，沮忠直之心，長壅蔽之漸，是為阻抑。

translations.literal: Our state has no specialized remonstrance office; now when other offices slightly offer proposals, they are called overstepping their place or called seeking a name, discouraging loyal uprightness and lengthening the gradual growth of obstruction—this is blocking and suppressing.
translations.idiomatic: Our state has no specialized remonstrance office; now when officials in other offices offer even slight proposals, they are called overstepping their place or seeking a name, discouraging loyal uprightness and deepening obstruction—this is blocking and suppressing.

sentences.zh: 其蠹六。

translations.literal: This is corruption the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth corruption.

sentences.zh: 自張居正蒙蔽主聰，道路以目，今余風未殄，欺罔日滋。

translations.literal: Since Zhang Juzheng blinded the ruler's keenness, people on the road met each other's eyes only with fear; today the lingering wind has not died out, and deception grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhang Juzheng blinded the ruler's keen perception, people on the road dared only glance at one another; the lingering influence has not yet died away, and deception grows daily.

sentences.zh: 如潘季馴之斥，大快人心，而猶累牘連章為之申雪，是為欺罔。

translations.literal: Such as Pan Jixun's dismissal, which greatly delighted the people, yet memorials still piled up one after another to clear his name—this is deception.
translations.idiomatic: When Pan Jixun was dismissed, the people rejoiced, yet memorials still piled up to clear his name—this is deception.

sentences.zh: 其蠹七。

translations.literal: This is corruption the seventh.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh corruption.

sentences.zh: 近中外臣僚或大臣交攻，或言官相訐，始以自用之私，終之好勝之習。

translations.literal: Recently civil and military officials within and without, whether great ministers attacking one another or remonstrating officials denouncing one another, begin from private self-use and end in the habit of loving victory.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, whether great ministers attacking one another or remonstrating officials denouncing one another, they begin from private self-interest and end in the habit of loving victory.

sentences.zh: 好勝不已，必致忿爭，忿爭不已，必致黨比。

translations.literal: Loving victory without end must lead to angry contention; angry contention without end must lead to factional alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Loving victory without end leads to angry contention; angry contention without end leads to factional alliance.

sentences.zh: 唐之牛、李，宋之洛、蜀，其初豈不由一言之相失哉？

translations.literal: Tang's Niu and Li factions, Song's Luoyang and Shu factions—did they not at the beginning arise from a single word's loss?
translations.idiomatic: The Niu and Li factions of Tang, the Luoyang and Shu factions of Song—did they not at first arise from a single word's loss?

sentences.zh: 是為競勝。

translations.literal: This is competing for victory.
translations.idiomatic: This is competing for victory.

sentences.zh: 其蠹八。

translations.literal: This is corruption the eighth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth corruption.

sentences.zh: 佞諛成風，日以浸甚。

translations.literal: Flattery and sycophancy have become the fashion and grow more intense day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery and sycophancy have become the fashion and grow more intense by the day.

sentences.zh: 言及大臣，則等之伊、傅；

translations.literal: When speaking of great ministers, they are equated with Yi Yin and Fu Yue;
translations.idiomatic: When speaking of great ministers, they are compared to Yi Yin and Fu Yue;

sentences.zh: 言及邊帥，則擬以方、召；

translations.literal: when speaking of frontier commanders, they are likened to Fang Shu and Zhao Bo;
translations.idiomatic: when speaking of frontier commanders, they are compared to Fang Shu and Zhao Bo;

sentences.zh: 言及中官，則誇呂、張復出；

translations.literal: when speaking of inner eunuchs, they boast that Lü Qiang and Zhang Yong have returned;
translations.idiomatic: when speaking of inner eunuchs, they boast that Lü Qiang and Zhang Yong have returned;

sentences.zh: 言及外吏，則頌卓、魯重生。

translations.literal: when speaking of outer officials, they praise that Zhuo Mao and Lu Su have been reborn.
translations.idiomatic: when speaking of outer officials, they praise Zhuo Mao and Lu Su as reborn.

sentences.zh: 非藉結歡，即因邀賂，是為佞諛。

translations.literal: If it is not by currying favor, it is by inviting bribes—this is flattery and sycophancy.
translations.idiomatic: Whether by currying favor or inviting bribes—this is flattery and sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 其蠹九。

translations.literal: This is corruption the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ninth corruption.

sentences.zh: 國家設官，各有常職。

translations.literal: The state establishes offices, each with its fixed duty.
translations.idiomatic: The state establishes offices, each with its fixed duty.

sentences.zh: 近兩京大臣，務建白以為名高，侵職掌而聽民訟。

translations.literal: Recently great ministers of the two capitals strive to make proposals for the sake of a lofty reputation, encroaching on others' jurisdictions and hearing the people's lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Recently great ministers in the two capitals strive to make proposals for the sake of reputation, encroaching on others' jurisdictions and hearing the people's lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 長告訐之風，失具瞻之體，是為乖戾。

translations.literal: They lengthen the wind of accusations and lose the dignity of being looked up to—this is perversity.
translations.idiomatic: They lengthen the wind of accusations and lose the dignity of being looked up to—this is perversity.

sentences.zh: 其蠹十也。

translations.literal: This is corruption the tenth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the tenth corruption.

sentences.zh: 懋學夙以直節著稱，其摘季馴不無過當。

translations.literal: Maoxue had long been famed for his upright integrity; in denouncing Jixun he was not without excess.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxue had long been famed for his upright integrity; in denouncing Jixun he was not without excess.

sentences.zh: 然所言好勝之弊，必成朋黨，後果如其言。

translations.literal: Yet what he said about the evil of loving victory necessarily forming factions afterward proved true, as events later confirmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what he said about the evil of loving victory necessarily forming factions proved true, as events later confirmed.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京戶部右侍郎，總理漕儲。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Right Vice Minister of Revenue in Nanjing and oversaw grain transport reserves.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to right vice minister of revenue in Nanjing and oversaw grain transport reserves.

sentences.zh: 疏白程任卿、江時之冤，二人遂得釋。

translations.literal: In a memorial he exposed the wrong done to Cheng Renqing and Jiang Shizhi, and the two men were thereupon released.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he exposed the injustice done to Cheng Renqing and Jiang Shizhi, and the two men were thereupon released.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以拾遺論罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was dismissed on account of a remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was dismissed on account of a remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚恭穆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the title Gongmu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the title Gongmu, "Respectful and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 張養蒙，字泰亨，澤州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yangmeng, style name Taiheng, was a native of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yangmeng, whose style was Taiheng, came from Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，歷吏科左給事中。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and rose through the posts to Left Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and rose through the posts to left supervising secretary in the personnel section.

sentences.zh: 少負才名，明習天下事。

translations.literal: In youth he bore a reputation for talent and was well versed in affairs under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he bore a reputation for talent and was well versed in affairs throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 居言職，慷慨好建白。

translations.literal: In his remonstrating office he was generous and fond of making proposals.
translations.idiomatic: In his remonstrating office he was generous and fond of making proposals.

sentences.zh: 以南北多水旱，條上治奸民、恤流民、愛富民三事，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: Because north and south suffered much from flood and drought, he set forth three matters: governing wicked people, relieving displaced people, and cherishing the prosperous people; the emperor praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Because north and south suffered much from flood and drought, he set forth three matters: governing wicked people, relieving displaced people, and cherishing the prosperous people; the emperor praised and accepted them.

sentences.zh: 錦衣都指揮羅秀營僉書，兵部尚書王遴格不行，失歡權要而去，秀竟夤緣得之。

translations.literal: Brocade Guard Chief Commander Luo Xiu sought a post as registrar; Minister of War Wang Lin rejected it and it did not go through; he lost the favor of powerful men and left office, yet Xiu ultimately obtained it through illicit connections.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade Guard chief commander Luo Xiu sought a post as registrar; Minister of War Wang Lin rejected it, and Lin lost the favor of powerful men and left office, yet Xiu ultimately obtained the post through illicit connections.

sentences.zh: 養蒙疏發其狀，事具遴傳。

translations.literal: Yangmeng submitted a memorial exposing the facts; the matter is given in full in Lin's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yangmeng submitted a memorial exposing the facts; the matter is given in full in Lin's biography.

sentences.zh: 御史高維崧等言事被謫，養蒙偕同官論救，復特疏訟之。

translations.literal: Censor Gao Weisong and others were demoted for remonstrating; Yangmeng joined colleagues in pleading for them and also submitted a special memorial on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gao Weisong and others were demoted for remonstrating; Yangmeng joined colleagues in pleading for them and also submitted a special memorial on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，奪俸。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will and had his salary stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the imperial will and had his salary stripped.

sentences.zh: 尋遷工科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Works Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to chief supervising secretary in the works section.

sentences.zh: 都御史潘季馴奏報河工，養蒙上言曰：「二十年來，河幾告患矣。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Pan Jixun memorialized reporting on river works; Yangmeng submitted a statement saying: For twenty years the river has nearly reported disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Pan Jixun memorialized reporting on river works; Yangmeng submitted a statement saying: "For twenty years the river has nearly reported disaster.

sentences.zh: 當其決，隨議塞，當其淤，隨議浚，事竣輒論功。

translations.literal: When it burst, proposals followed to block it; when it silted, proposals followed to dredge it; when the work was finished merit was at once discussed.
translations.idiomatic: When it burst, proposals followed to block it; when it silted, proposals followed to dredge it; when the work was finished merit was at once discussed.

sentences.zh: 夫淤決則委之天災而不任其咎，浚塞則歸之人事而共蒙其賞。

translations.literal: When silting and bursting occurred, they were attributed to heaven's disaster and blame was not borne; when dredging and blocking succeeded, they were attributed to human effort and all shared the reward.
translations.idiomatic: When silting and bursting occurred, they were attributed to heaven's disaster and blame was not borne; when dredging and blocking succeeded, they were attributed to human effort and all shared the reward.

sentences.zh: 及報成未久，懼有後虞，急求謝事，而繼者復告患矣。

translations.literal: When the report of completion had not long been made, fearing later trouble, they hurried to request leave, and their successors again reported disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When the report of completion had not long been made, fearing later trouble, they hurried to request leave, and their successors again reported disaster.

sentences.zh: 其故皆由不久任也。

translations.literal: The reason for all this was that office was not held long.
translations.idiomatic: The reason for all this was that office was not held long.

sentences.zh: 夫官不久任，其弊有三：後先異時也，人己異見也，功罪難執也。

translations.literal: When office is not held long, there are three evils: later and earlier differ in time, self and other differ in views, and merit and guilt are hard to fix.
translations.idiomatic: When office is not held long, there are three evils: later and earlier differ in time, self and other differ in views, and merit and guilt are hard to fix.

sentences.zh: 請仿邊臣例，增秩久任，斯職守專而可責成功。」

translations.literal: I beg that the precedent of frontier officials be followed, rank be increased and tenure prolonged, so that duties may be specialized and success can be required.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the precedent of frontier officials be followed, rank be increased and tenure prolonged, so that duties may be specialized and success can be required.

sentences.zh: 帝深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply approved.

sentences.zh: 有詔潞安進綢二千四百匹。

translations.literal: There was an edict that Lu'an present two thousand four hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: There was an edict that Lu'an present two thousand four hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復命增五千。

translations.literal: Before long, an order came again to increase it by five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, an order came again to increase it by five thousand.

sentences.zh: 養蒙率同官力爭，且曰：「從來傳奉職造，具題者內臣，擬旨者閣臣，抄發者科臣。

translations.literal: Yangmeng led colleagues in forceful protest and also said: From former times, for missions of the transmission service, the one who presented the topic was an inner eunuch, the one who drafted the rescript was a grand secretary, and the one who copied and issued it was a supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Yangmeng led colleagues in forceful protest and also said: "From former times, for missions of the transmission service, the one who presented the topic was an inner eunuch, the one who drafted the rescript was a grand secretary, and the one who copied and issued it was a supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 今徑下部，非祖制。」

translations.literal: Now it goes directly to the ministry—this is not the ancestral system.
translations.idiomatic: Now it goes directly to the ministry—this is not the ancestral system.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: This was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: This was not followed.

sentences.zh: 出為河南右參政。

translations.literal: He went out as Right Vice Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as right vice administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 尋召為太仆少卿，四遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was soon summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and was promoted four times to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and was promoted four times to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，極諫時政闕失，言：

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he remonstrated to the utmost on the failures of current policy and said:
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he remonstrated forcefully on the failures of current policy and said:

sentences.zh: 邇來殿廷希禦，上下不交。

translations.literal: Recently in the palace hall people court favor; above and below do not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: Recently in the palace hall people court favor; above and below do not communicate.

sentences.zh: 或疑外臣不可盡信，或疑外事未可盡從。

translations.literal: Some suspect that outer officials cannot all be trusted, or suspect that outer affairs cannot all be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Some suspect that outer officials cannot all be trusted, or suspect that outer affairs cannot all be followed.

sentences.zh: 君臣相猜，政事積廢。

translations.literal: Ruler and ministers suspect one another, and government affairs pile up in neglect.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers suspect one another, and government affairs pile up in neglect.

sentences.zh: 致市猾得以揣意旨，左右得以播威權。

translations.literal: Thus market sharpers are able to probe intent, and those at the ruler's side are able to spread authority.
translations.idiomatic: Thus market sharpers are able to probe intent, and those at the ruler's side are able to spread authority.

sentences.zh: 惟利是聞，禍將胡底。

translations.literal: They heed only profit; disaster will have no bottom.
translations.idiomatic: They heed only profit; disaster will have no bottom.

sentences.zh: 謹以三輕二重之弊為陛下陳之。

translations.literal: I respectfully set forth for Your Majesty the evils of three lightened and two weighted.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully set forth for Your Majesty the evils of three lightened and two weighted.

sentences.zh: 一、部院之體漸輕。

translations.literal: First, the stature of ministries and courts has gradually lightened.
translations.idiomatic: First, the stature of ministries and courts has gradually lightened.

sentences.zh: 或虛其位而不補，或用其人而不任。

translations.literal: Sometimes the post is left vacant and not filled, sometimes the man is used but not entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the post is left vacant and not filled, sometimes the man is used but not entrusted.

sentences.zh: 如冬官一曹，亞卿專署，已為異事，乃冢宰何官，數月虛位。

translations.literal: In the Works Section, a vice minister alone signs documents—already an anomaly—yet the post of Minister of Personnel has stood vacant for months.
translations.idiomatic: In the Works Section, a vice minister alone signs documents—already an anomaly—yet the post of minister of personnel has stood vacant for months.

sentences.zh: 法司議劉世延罪，竟爾留中，主事劉冠南疏入即發。

translations.literal: The law offices discussed Liu Shiyan's crime, yet it was held in the palace; when Principal Secretary Liu Guannan submitted a memorial it was at once issued.
translations.idiomatic: The law offices discussed Liu Shiyan's crime, yet it was held in the palace; when principal secretary Liu Guannan submitted a memorial it was at once issued.

sentences.zh: 何小臣聽而大臣不聽，單疏下而公疏不下哉！

translations.literal: Why are small officials heard while great ministers are not heard, single memorials issued while joint memorials are not issued!
translations.idiomatic: Why are small officials heard while great ministers are not heard, single memorials issued while joint memorials are not issued!

sentences.zh: 以至戶曹三疏諫開礦，臣院九疏催行取，皆置不報。

translations.literal: To the point that the Revenue Section submitted three memorials remonstrating against opening mines, and our court submitted nine memorials urging selections, yet all were left unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: To the point that the Revenue Section submitted three memorials remonstrating against opening mines, and our court submitted nine memorials urging selections, yet all were left unanswered.

sentences.zh: 議大事則十疏而九不行，遇廷推則十人而九不用。

translations.literal: When great affairs are discussed, nine of ten memorials do not go through; when court recommendations are made, nine of ten men are not used.
translations.idiomatic: When great affairs are discussed, nine of ten memorials do not go through; when court recommendations are made, nine of ten men are not used.

sentences.zh: 失大臣師表百僚，奈何輕之至此！

translations.literal: Great ministers lose their role as models for the hundred officials—how can they be lightened to this point!
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers lose their role as models for the hundred officials—how can they be lightened to this point!

sentences.zh: 一、科道之職漸輕。

translations.literal: Second, the office of censors and supervising secretaries has gradually lightened.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the office of censors and supervising secretaries has gradually lightened.

sentences.zh: 五科都給事中久虛不補，御史曹學程一系不釋，考選臺諫，屢請屢格，乃至服闋補任，亦皆廢閣。

translations.literal: The five sections' chief supervising secretaries have long stood vacant without filling; censor Cao Xuecheng has long been held without release; selection of censors and remonstrators has been repeatedly requested and repeatedly blocked, even when mourning leave ended and reappointments were due, all were shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The five sections' chief supervising secretaries have long stood vacant without filling; censor Cao Xuecheng has long been held without release; selection of censors and remonstrators has been repeatedly requested and repeatedly blocked, even when mourning leave ended and reappointments were due, all were shelved.

sentences.zh: 是不欲言路之充也。

translations.literal: This shows that the remonstrance route is not wished to be filled.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the remonstrance route is not wished to be filled.

sentences.zh: 夫政無缺失，何憚人言。

translations.literal: When government has no failures, why fear men's words?
translations.idiomatic: When government has no failures, why fear men's words?

sentences.zh: 徒使唯諾風成，謇諤意絕，國是將何定乎？

translations.literal: They only make the wind of yes-men grow and the intent of outspoken integrity die—how will the state's affairs be settled?
translations.idiomatic: They only make the wind of yes-men grow and the intent of outspoken integrity die—how will the state's affairs be settled?

sentences.zh: 一、撫按之任漸輕。

translations.literal: Third, the responsibility of grand coordinators and touring censors has gradually lightened.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the responsibility of grand coordinators and touring censors has gradually lightened.

sentences.zh: 如開礦一事，撫按有言，鹹蒙切責。

translations.literal: In the matter of opening mines, when grand coordinators and touring censors spoke, all received sharp rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: In the matter of opening mines, when grand coordinators and touring censors spoke, all received sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 於是鄭一麟以千戶而妄劾李盛春。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zheng Yilin, a company commander, rashly impeached Li Shengchun.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zheng Yilin, a company commander, rashly impeached Li Shengchun.

sentences.zh: 夫閽人、武弁得以制巡撫之命，紀綱不倒置乎？

translations.literal: When gatekeepers and military officers can control a grand coordinator's orders, are regulations not turned upside down?
translations.idiomatic: When gatekeepers and military officers can control a grand coordinator's orders, are regulations not turned upside down?

sentences.zh: 一珰得誌，諸珰效尤，撫按斂手，何有於監司？

translations.literal: One eunuch gets his way and the other eunuchs follow his example; grand coordinators and touring censors fold their hands—what is left for surveillance commissioners?
translations.idiomatic: One eunuch gets his way and the other eunuchs follow his example; grand coordinators and touring censors fold their hands—what is left for surveillance commissioners?

sentences.zh: 從此陛下之赤子將無人拊循矣。

translations.literal: From this Your Majesty's common people will have no one to comfort and guide them.
translations.idiomatic: From this Your Majesty's common people will have no one to comfort and guide them.

sentences.zh: 一、進獻之途漸重。

translations.literal: First, the path of presenting tribute has gradually weighted.
translations.idiomatic: First, the path of presenting tribute has gradually weighted.

sentences.zh: 下僚捐俸，儒士獻資，名為助工，實懷覬幸。

translations.literal: Lower officials donate salary, Confucian scholars present funds, in name to aid the works but in fact harboring hope of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lower officials donate salary, Confucian scholars present funds, in name to aid the works but in fact harboring hope of favor.

sentences.zh: 甚者百戶王守仁以謀復世爵，妄構楚府，而使陛下恩薄於懿親；

translations.literal: Still worse, company commander Wang Shouren, seeking to recover a hereditary enfeoffment, rashly framed the Chu princely house, making Your Majesty's grace thin toward close kin;
translations.idiomatic: Still worse, company commander Wang Shouren, seeking to recover a hereditary enfeoffment, rashly framed the Chu princely house, making Your Majesty's grace thin toward close kin;

sentences.zh: 主簿張以述以求復舊秩，妄獻白鹿，而使陛下德損於玩物。

translations.literal: registrar Zhang Yishu, seeking to recover his former rank, rashly presented a white deer, making Your Majesty's virtue diminished by fondness for curios.
translations.idiomatic: registrar Zhang Yishu, seeking to recover his former rank, rashly presented a white deer, making Your Majesty's virtue diminished by fondness for curios.

sentences.zh: 部臣糾之不聽，言官糾之不聽，業已明示好惡，大開受獻之門。

translations.literal: Ministry officials impeached them but were not heard; remonstrating officials impeached them but were not heard; already preference and aversion have been openly shown and the gate of receiving presentations widely opened.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials impeached them but were not heard; remonstrating officials impeached them but were not heard; already preference and aversion have been openly shown and the gate of receiving presentations widely opened.

sentences.zh: 將見媚子宵人，投袂競起，今日獻靈瑞，明日貢珍奇，究使敗節文官、僨軍武帥，憑藉錢神，邀求故物，不至如嘉靖末年之濁亂不止也。

translations.literal: We shall see fawning sons and night people fling up their sleeves and compete: today presenting spiritual omens, tomorrow presenting rare curiosities, until corrupt civil officials and failed military commanders, relying on the money god, seek former things—until it does not stop short of the foul disorder of the late Jiajing years.
translations.idiomatic: We shall see fawning sons and night people fling up their sleeves and compete: today presenting spiritual omens, tomorrow presenting rare curiosities, until corrupt civil officials and failed military commanders, relying on the money god, seek former things—until it does not stop short of the foul disorder of the late Jiajing years.

sentences.zh: 一、內差之勢漸重。

translations.literal: Second, the power of inner missions has gradually weighted.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the power of inner missions has gradually weighted.

sentences.zh: 中使紛然四出，乞請之章無日不上，批答之旨無言不溫。

translations.literal: Inner envoys swarm forth in all directions; petitions for requests have no day without ascending; rescripts of reply have no word without warmth.
translations.idiomatic: Inner envoys swarm forth in all directions; petitions for requests have no day without ascending; rescripts of reply have no word without warmth.

sentences.zh: 左右藉武弁以營差，武弁藉左右以網利，共構狂言，誑惑天聽。

translations.literal: Those at the side rely on military officers to seek missions; military officers rely on those at the side to net profit; together they fabricate wild words and deceive heaven's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Those at the side rely on military officers to seek missions; military officers rely on those at the side to net profit; together they fabricate wild words and deceive heaven's hearing.

sentences.zh: 陛下方厭外臣沮撓，謂欲辦家事，必賴家奴，於是有言無不立聽。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just then weary of outer officials' obstruction and says that to manage household affairs one must rely on household servants; therefore whatever is said is at once heard.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is just then weary of outer officials' obstruction and says that to manage household affairs one must rely on household servants; therefore whatever is said is at once heard.

sentences.zh: 豈武弁皆急君，而朝紳盡誤國乎？

translations.literal: Are military officers all urgent for the ruler while court gentry all harm the state?
translations.idiomatic: Are military officers all urgent for the ruler while court gentry all harm the state?

sentences.zh: 今奸宄實繁有徒。

translations.literal: Now villains are indeed numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Now villains are indeed numerous.

sentences.zh: 采礦不已，必及采珠；

translations.literal: Mining without end must reach pearl gathering;
translations.idiomatic: Mining without end must reach pearl gathering;

sentences.zh: 皇店不止，漸及皇莊。

translations.literal: imperial shops do not stop and gradually reach imperial estates.
translations.idiomatic: imperial shops do not stop and gradually reach imperial estates.

sentences.zh: 繼而營市舶，繼而復鎮守，內可以謀坐營，外可以謀監軍。

translations.literal: Then managing maritime trade, then restoring garrison commanders—within they can scheme to sit in camp, without they can scheme to supervise armies.
translations.idiomatic: Then managing maritime trade, then restoring garrison commanders—within they can scheme to sit in camp, without they can scheme to supervise armies.

sentences.zh: 正德敝風，其鑒不遠。

translations.literal: The corrupt wind of the Zhengde reign—its mirror is not far.
translations.idiomatic: The corrupt wind of the Zhengde reign—its mirror is not far.

sentences.zh: 凡此三輕二重，勢每相因。

translations.literal: All these three lightened and two weighted—the momentum each time mutually causes.
translations.idiomatic: All these three lightened and two weighted—the momentum each time mutually causes.

sentences.zh: 德與財不並立，中與外不兩勝，惟陛下早見而速圖之。

translations.literal: Virtue and wealth cannot stand together, inner and outer cannot both win; may Your Majesty see this early and plan swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue and wealth cannot stand together, inner and outer cannot both win; may Your Majesty see this early and plan swiftly.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: There was no reply.

sentences.zh: 又明年六月，兩宮三殿繼災。

translations.literal: Again in the sixth month of the following year, the two palaces and three halls suffered fire in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Again in the sixth month of the following year, the two palaces and three halls suffered fire in succession.

sentences.zh: 養蒙復上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yangmeng again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yangmeng again submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 近日之災，前古未有。

translations.literal: The recent disaster has no precedent in former antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The recent disaster has no precedent in former antiquity.

sentences.zh: 自非君臣交儆，痛革敝風，恐虛文相謾，大禍必至。

translations.literal: If ruler and ministers do not mutually warn one another and painfully reform the corrupt wind, I fear empty words will deceive one another and great disaster must arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Unless ruler and ministers warn one another and painfully reform the corrupt customs, empty words will deceive one another and great disaster is sure to come.

sentences.zh: 臣請陛下躬謁郊廟以謝嚴譴，立禦便殿以通物情，早建國本以系人心。

translations.literal: Your subject begs Your Majesty personally to visit the suburban altars and temples to apologize for stern punishment, establish an imperial hall for convenience to communicate with things and feelings, and early establish the heir to bind men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty personally to visit the suburban altars and temples to apologize for stern punishment, establish an imperial hall for convenience to communicate with the realm, and early establish the heir to bind men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 停銀礦、皇店之役，杜四海亂階；

translations.literal: Stop the labor of silver mines and imperial shops to block the sources of disorder throughout the four seas;
translations.idiomatic: Stop the labor of silver mines and imperial shops to block the sources of disorder throughout the realm;

sentences.zh: 減宦官宮妾之刑，弭蕭墻隱禍。

translations.literal: reduce punishments of eunuchs and palace women to quell hidden disaster within the palace walls.
translations.idiomatic: reduce punishments of eunuchs and palace women to quell hidden disaster within the palace walls.

sentences.zh: 然此皆應天實事，猶非應天實心也。

translations.literal: Yet all these are real deeds in responding to Heaven, and are still not the real heart in responding to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all these are real deeds in responding to Heaven, and are still not the real heart in responding to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 罪己不如正己，格事不如格心。

translations.literal: Blaming oneself is not as good as correcting oneself; correcting affairs is not as good as correcting the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Blaming oneself is not as good as correcting oneself; correcting affairs is not as good as correcting the heart.

sentences.zh: 陛下平日成心有四：一曰好逸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty on ordinary days has four fixed intentions: first, love of ease.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty on ordinary days has four fixed intentions: first, love of ease.

sentences.zh: 朝享倦於躬臨，章奏倦於省覽。

translations.literal: Court sacrifices weary of attending in person, memorials weary of reviewing.
translations.idiomatic: Court sacrifices weary of attending in person, memorials weary of reviewing.

sentences.zh: 古帝王乾健不息，似不如此。

translations.literal: The ancient emperors were qian and vigorous without ceasing—this seems not to be so.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient emperors were vigorous without ceasing—this seems not to be so.

sentences.zh: 一曰好疑。

translations.literal: Second, love of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Second, love of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 疑及近侍，則左右莫必其生；

translations.literal: When suspicion reaches close attendants, then those at the side cannot be sure of their lives;
translations.idiomatic: When suspicion reaches close attendants, then those at the side cannot be sure of their lives;

sentences.zh: 疑及外庭，則僚采不安於位。

translations.literal: when suspicion reaches the outer court, then colleagues are not secure in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: when suspicion reaches the outer court, then colleagues are not secure in their posts.

sentences.zh: 究且謀以疑敗，奸以疑容。

translations.literal: In the end plots fail through suspicion, and villains are harbored through suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: In the end plots fail through suspicion, and villains are harbored through suspicion.

sentences.zh: 古帝王至誠馭物，似不如此。

translations.literal: The ancient emperors governed things with utmost sincerity—this seems not to be so.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient emperors governed things with utmost sincerity—this seems not to be so.

sentences.zh: 一曰好勝。

translations.literal: Third, love of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Third, love of victory.

sentences.zh: 奮厲威嚴以震群工，喜諂諛而惡鯁直，厭封駁而樂順從。

translations.literal: Exerting fierce authority and sternness to shake the hundred officials, loving flattery and hating blunt uprightness, tiring of sealed remonstrance and delighting in compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Exerting fierce authority and sternness to shake the hundred officials, loving flattery and hating blunt uprightness, tiring of sealed remonstrance and delighting in compliance.

sentences.zh: 古帝王予違汝弼，似不如此。

translations.literal: The ancient emperors, when you err I assist you—this seems not to be so.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient emperors said, when you err I assist you—this seems not to be so.

sentences.zh: 一曰好貨。

translations.literal: Fourth, love of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, love of goods.

sentences.zh: 以聚斂為奉公，以投獻為盡節。

translations.literal: Taking exaction as serving the public, taking presentations as utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Taking exaction as serving the public, taking presentations as utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 古帝王四海為家，似不如此。

translations.literal: The ancient emperors took the four seas as home—this seems not to be so.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient emperors took the four seas as home—this seems not to be so.

sentences.zh: 願陛下戒此四者，亟圖更張，庶天意可回，國祚可保。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty guard against these four and swiftly plan renewal, so that Heaven's intent may turn and the state's fortune may be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty guard against these four and swiftly plan renewal, so that Heaven's intent may turn and the state's fortune may be preserved.

sentences.zh: 帝亦不省。

translations.literal: The emperor also did not reflect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also did not reflect.

sentences.zh: 尋遷戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to right vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 時再用師朝鮮，命養蒙督餉。

translations.literal: At that time troops were again used in Korea, and Yangmeng was ordered to supervise provisions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time troops were again used in Korea, and Yangmeng was ordered to supervise provisions.

sentences.zh: 事寧，予一子官。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, one son was granted office.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, one son was granted office.

sentences.zh: 三十年，尚書陳蕖稱疾乞罷。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year Minister Chen Lian claimed illness and begged to resign.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year Minister Chen Lian claimed illness and begged to resign.

sentences.zh: 詔養蒙署事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yangmeng to act as head of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yangmeng to act as head of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 會養蒙亦有疾在告，固辭。

translations.literal: As Yangmeng also had illness and was on leave, he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: As Yangmeng also had illness and was on leave, he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 給事中夏子陽劾其托疾，遂罷歸。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Xia Ziyang impeached him for feigning illness, and he was thereupon dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Xia Ziyang impeached him for feigning illness, and he was thereupon dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，賜謚毅敏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was granted the posthumous title Yimin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was granted the posthumous title Yimin, "Resolute and Keen."

sentences.zh: 孟一脈，字淑孔，東阿人。

translations.literal: Meng Yimai, style name Shukong, was a native of Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yimai, whose style was Shukong, came from Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 為平遙知縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Pingyao.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Pingyao.

sentences.zh: 以廉能擢南京御史。

translations.literal: For integrity and ability he was promoted to Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: For integrity and ability he was promoted to censor in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 萬歷六年五月，上言：「近上兩宮徽號，覃恩內外，獨御史傅應禎、進士鄒元標、部郎艾穆、沈思孝，投荒萬里，遠絕親闈，非所以廣錫類溥仁施也。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Wanli he submitted a statement saying: Recently the two palaces received honorific titles, grace was extended within and without, yet alone Censor Fu Yingzhen, jinshi Zou Yuanbiao, and department secretaries Ai Mu and Shen Sixiao were cast into the wilderness ten thousand li, far cut off from kin—this is not how to extend grace broadly and apply benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year of the Wanli reign he submitted a statement saying: "Recently the two palaces received honorific titles and grace was extended within and without, yet alone Censor Fu Yingzhen, Jinshi Zou Yuanbiao, and department secretaries Ai Mu and Shen Sixiao were cast into exile ten thousand li away, far cut off from kin—this is not how to extend grace broadly and apply benevolence.

sentences.zh: 疏入，忤張居正，黜為民。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it offended Zhang Juzheng and he was dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial entered, it offended Zhang Juzheng and he was dismissed as a commoner."

sentences.zh: 居正死，起故官，疏陳五事，言：

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, he was raised to his former office and memorialized setting forth five matters, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng died, he was raised to his former office and memorialized setting forth five matters, saying:

sentences.zh: 近再選宮女至九十七人，急征一時，輦下甚擾。

translations.literal: Recently palace women were again selected to ninety-seven persons; they were urgently summoned at one time and the capital was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Recently palace women were again selected to ninety-seven persons; they were urgently summoned at one time and the capital was greatly disturbed.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: This is the first.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first.

sentences.zh: 中外章奏，宜下部臣議覆，閣臣擬旨，脫有不當，臺諫得糾駁之。

translations.literal: Memorials within and without should be sent to ministry officials for discussion and reply, grand secretaries to draft rescripts; if there is impropriety, censors and remonstrators may impeach and reject.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials within and without should be sent to ministry officials for discussion and reply, grand secretaries to draft rescripts; if there is impropriety, censors and remonstrators may impeach and reject.

sentences.zh: 今乃不任臣工，顓取宸斷，明旨一出，臣下莫敢犯顏。

translations.literal: Now officials are not entrusted; the ruler alone takes the imperial decision; once a clear edict issues, ministers below dare not offend the countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Now officials are not entrusted; the ruler alone takes the imperial decision; once a clear edict issues, ministers below dare not offend the countenance.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: This is the second.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second.

sentences.zh: 士習邪正，系世道汙隆。

translations.literal: Whether scholar-custom is wicked or upright is tied to whether the age is foul or flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Whether scholar-custom is wicked or upright is tied to whether the age is foul or flourishing.

sentences.zh: 今廉恥日喪，營求茍且。

translations.literal: Now integrity and shame daily decline and scrambling for survival grows.
translations.idiomatic: Now integrity and shame daily decline and scrambling for survival grows.

sentences.zh: 亟宜更化救弊，先實行而後才華。

translations.literal: One should urgently reform and save abuses, first practical conduct and afterward talent.
translations.idiomatic: One should urgently reform and save abuses, first practical conduct and afterward talent.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: This is the third.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third.

sentences.zh: 東南財賦之區，靡於淫巧，民力竭矣，非陛下有以倡之乎？

translations.literal: The southeast, a region of wealth and taxes, is wasted on extravagant craft; the people's strength is exhausted—is it not that Your Majesty has led them?
translations.idiomatic: The southeast, a region of wealth and taxes, is wasted on extravagant craft; the people's strength is exhausted—is it not that Your Majesty has led them?

sentences.zh: 數年以來，禦用不給。

translations.literal: For several years imperial use has not sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: For several years imperial use has not sufficed.

sentences.zh: 今日取之光祿，明日取之太仆，浮梁之磁，南海之珠，玩好之奇，器用之巧，日新月異。

translations.literal: Today it is taken from the Court of Imperial Entertainments, tomorrow from the Court of the Imperial Stud; porcelain from Fuliang, pearls from the southern sea, curious playthings, ingenious vessels and implements—new day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is taken from the Court of Imperial Entertainments, tomorrow from the Court of the Imperial Stud; porcelain from Fuliang, pearls from the southern sea, curious playthings, ingenious vessels and implements—new day by day.

sentences.zh: 遇聖節則有壽服，元宵則有燈服，端陽則有五毒吉服，年例則有歲進龍服。

translations.literal: On the sage's birthday there are longevity robes, on the Lantern Festival lamp robes, on the Dragon Boat Festival five-poison auspicious robes, on the annual precedent there are yearly tribute dragon robes.
translations.idiomatic: On the sage's birthday there are longevity robes, on the Lantern Festival lamp robes, on the Dragon Boat Festival five-poison auspicious robes, on the annual precedent there are yearly tribute dragon robes.

sentences.zh: 以至覃恩錫賚，小大畢沾；

translations.literal: Even extending grace with gifts, great and small all receive;
translations.idiomatic: Even extending grace with gifts, great and small all receive;

sentences.zh: 謁陵犒賜，耗費巨萬。

translations.literal: visiting tombs and bestowing rewards consume tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: visiting tombs and bestowing rewards consume tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 錙銖取之，泥沙用之。

translations.literal: Taken by the ounce, used like sand.
translations.idiomatic: Taken by the ounce, used like sand.

sentences.zh: 於是民間習為麗侈，窮耳目之好，竭工藝之能，不知紀極。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people learn gorgeous extravagance, exhausting what delights eye and ear and depleting craft to the limit, knowing no measure.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the people learn gorgeous extravagance, exhausting what delights eye and ear and depleting craft to the limit, knowing no measure.

sentences.zh: 夫中人得十金，即足供終歲之用。

translations.literal: A man of moderate means obtaining ten ounces of gold is enough to supply a whole year's use.
translations.idiomatic: A man of moderate means obtaining ten ounces of gold is enough to supply a whole year's use.

sentences.zh: 今一物而常兼中人數家之產。

translations.literal: Now one object often equals the property of several moderate households.
translations.idiomatic: Now one object often equals the property of several moderate households.

sentences.zh: 或刻沈檀，鏤犀象，以珠寶金玉飾之。

translations.literal: Some carve eaglewood and sandalwood, carve rhinoceros and ivory, and adorn them with pearls, gems, gold, and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Some carve eaglewood and sandalwood, carve rhinoceros and ivory, and adorn them with pearls, gems, gold, and jade.

sentences.zh: 周鼎、商彜、秦鉈、漢鑒，皆搜求於海內。

translations.literal: Zhou tripods, Shang vessels, Qin bells, and Han mirrors are all sought throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou tripods, Shang vessels, Qin bells, and Han mirrors are all sought throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 窮歲月之力，專一器之工；

translations.literal: Exhausting years of effort on the craft of a single vessel;
translations.idiomatic: Exhausting years of effort on the craft of a single vessel;

sentences.zh: 罄生平之資，取一盼之適。

translations.literal: spending a lifetime's resources to obtain one moment's pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: spending a lifetime's resources to obtain one moment's pleasure.

sentences.zh: 殊不知財賄易盡，嗜欲無窮。

translations.literal: They do not know that wealth is easily exhausted and desire has no end.
translations.idiomatic: They do not know that wealth is easily exhausted and desire has no end.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能恭儉節約以先天下，禁彼浮淫，還之貞樸，則財用自裕，而風俗亦淳。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can with respect and frugality take the lead under Heaven, forbid that floating excess, and return to simplicity, then wealth will naturally suffice and custom will also be pure.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty can with respect and frugality take the lead under Heaven, forbid that floating excess, and return to simplicity, then wealth will naturally suffice and custom will also be pure.

sentences.zh: 四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 邊疆之臣，日弛戎備，上下蒙蔽，莫以實聞。

translations.literal: Frontier officials daily relax military preparedness; above and below conceal one another and nothing real is reported.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials daily relax military preparedness; above and below conceal one another and nothing real is reported.

sentences.zh: 由邊臣相繼為本兵，題覆處分，盡在其口。

translations.literal: Because frontier officials in succession become ministers of war, discussion and disposition of memorial replies are all in their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Because frontier officials in succession become ministers of war, discussion and disposition of memorial replies are all in their mouths.

sentences.zh: 言出而中傷隨之，誰肯為無益之談，自取禍敗哉？

translations.literal: When words issue, wounding follows—who will speak useless talk and invite disaster?
translations.idiomatic: When words issue, wounding follows—who will speak useless talk and invite disaster?

sentences.zh: 漁夫舍餌以得魚，未聞以餌養魚者也。

translations.literal: A fisherman abandons bait to obtain fish; I have never heard of feeding fish with bait.
translations.idiomatic: A fisherman abandons bait to obtain fish; I have never heard of feeding fish with bait.

sentences.zh: 今以中國之文帛綺繡為蕃戎常服，雖曰貢市，實則媚之。

translations.literal: Now China's silks, brocades, and fine weave are the regular dress of the frontier tribes; though called tribute markets, in fact they flatter.
translations.idiomatic: Now China's silks, brocades, and fine weave are the regular dress of the frontier tribes; though called tribute markets, in fact they flatter.

sentences.zh: 邊臣假貢市以賂戎，戎人肆剽竊而要我。

translations.literal: Frontier officials use tribute markets to bribe the tribes; the tribes wildly plunder and demand from us.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials use tribute markets to bribe the tribes; the tribes wildly plunder and demand from us.

sentences.zh: 彼此相欺，以誑君父。

translations.literal: Each deceives the other to deceive ruler and father.
translations.idiomatic: Each deceives the other to deceive ruler and father.

sentences.zh: 幸其不來，來則莫禦。

translations.literal: They pray they do not come; when they come none can resist.
translations.idiomatic: They pray they do not come; when they come none can resist.

sentences.zh: 所謂以餌養魚者也。

translations.literal: This is what is called feeding fish with bait.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called feeding fish with bait.

sentences.zh: 請明詔樞臣，洗心易慮。

translations.literal: I beg a clear edict to the military ministers to wash the heart and change thought.
translations.idiomatic: I beg a clear edict to the military ministers to wash the heart and change thought.

sentences.zh: 戰守之備，一一講求，付之邊臣。

translations.literal: Preparations for war and defense should be discussed one by one and entrusted to frontier officials.
translations.idiomatic: Preparations for war and defense should be discussed one by one and entrusted to frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 使將識敵情，兵識將意，庶乎臂指如意，國可無虞。

translations.literal: Let generals know the enemy's situation and soldiers know the general's intent—then perhaps arm and finger will be as one wishes and the state may be without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Let generals know the enemy's situation and soldiers know the general's intent—then perhaps arm and finger will be as one wishes and the state may be without worry.

sentences.zh: 五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth.
