sentences.zh: 疏入，忤旨，謫建昌推官。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it offended the imperial will and he was demoted to reviewing official of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial entered, it offended the imperial will and he was demoted to reviewing official of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 屢遷南京右通政。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Right Vice Commissioner of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to right vice commissioner of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on account of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，起右僉都御史，巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was raised as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he was raised as right assistant censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.

sentences.zh: 居三年，廷推左副都御史。

translations.literal: After three years, court recommendation made him Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, court recommendation made him left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 未得命，給事中官應震論其縱子驕恣。

translations.literal: Before the appointment was received, supervising secretary Guan Yingzhen discussed his indulging his son's arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointment was received, supervising secretary Guan Yingzhen discussed his indulging his son's arrogance.

sentences.zh: 疏雖留中，一脈竟引疾去。

translations.literal: Although the memorial was held in the palace, Yimai ultimately cited illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Although the memorial was held in the palace, Yimai ultimately cited illness and left.

sentences.zh: 年八十一卒。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 一脈初以直諫著聲。

translations.literal: Yimai at first was famed for his voice in blunt remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Yimai at first was famed for his voice in blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 晚膺節鉞，年力已衰，不克有所表樹雲。

translations.literal: Late in life he received command authority; his years and strength had already declined and he could not achieve notable deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he received command authority; his years and strength had already declined and he could not achieve notable deeds.

sentences.zh: 何士晉，字武莪，宜興人。

translations.literal: He Shijin, style name Wu'e, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He Shijin, whose style was Wu'e, came from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 父其孝，得士晉晚。

translations.literal: His father Qi Xiao obtained Shijin late in life.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi Xiao obtained Shijin late in life.

sentences.zh: 族子利其資，結黨致之死。

translations.literal: A clansman coveted his property, formed a faction, and brought about his death.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman coveted his property, formed a faction, and brought about his death.

sentences.zh: 繼母吳氏匿士晉外家。

translations.literal: His stepmother, the Lady Wu, hid Shijin at her natal family.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother, Lady Wu, hid Shijin at her natal family.

sentences.zh: 讀書稍懈，母輒示以父血衣。

translations.literal: When he slackened slightly in study, his mother would show him his father's blood-stained garment.
translations.idiomatic: When he slackened slightly in study, his mother would show him his father's blood-stained garment.

sentences.zh: 士晉感厲，與人言，未嘗有笑容。

translations.literal: Shijin was moved and stimulated; in speaking with others he never had a smiling countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Shijin was moved and stimulated; in speaking with others he never had a smiling countenance.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十六年舉進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of the Wanli reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 持血衣訴之官，罪人皆抵法。

translations.literal: He carried the blood garment and sued at court; the guilty all met the law.
translations.idiomatic: He carried the blood garment and sued at court; the guilty all met the law.

sentences.zh: 初授寧波推官，擢工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was first appointed reviewing official of Ningbo and was promoted to supervising secretary of the Works Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed reviewing official of Ningbo and was promoted to supervising secretary in the works section.

sentences.zh: 首疏請通章奏、緩聚斂。

translations.literal: His first memorial requested that memorials pass through and exactions be eased.
translations.idiomatic: His first memorial requested that memorials pass through and exactions be eased.

sentences.zh: 俄言：「袞職有闕，廷臣言雖逆耳，每荷優容。

translations.literal: Soon he said: There is a vacancy in the imperial robe; court ministers' words, though harsh to the ear, each receive gracious forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he said: "There is a vacancy in the imperial robe; court ministers' words, though harsh to the ear, each receive gracious forbearance.

sentences.zh: 獨論及輔臣，必欲借主威以泄憤。

translations.literal: Only when discussing assisting ministers must they borrow the ruler's authority to vent anger.
translations.idiomatic: Only when discussing assisting ministers must they borrow the ruler's authority to vent anger.

sentences.zh: 是陛下負拒諫之名，輔臣收固寵之實，天下所以積憤輔臣而不能平也。

translations.literal: This is Your Majesty bearing the name of rejecting remonstrance, assisting ministers receiving the substance of securing favor, and the reason the realm accumulates anger at assisting ministers and cannot be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: This is Your Majesty bearing the name of rejecting remonstrance, assisting ministers receiving the substance of securing favor, and the reason the realm accumulates anger at assisting ministers and cannot be at peace.

sentences.zh: 如孫幰、郭子章、戴耀、沈子木，宜舍不舍，公論乖違，輔臣賡安得不任其咎？」

translations.literal: As with Sun Huan, Guo Zizhang, Dai Yao, and Shen Zimu—those who ought to have been dismissed were not dismissed, public opinion was violated, and the assisting ministers linger on in office; how can they not bear the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Sun Huan, Guo Zizhang, Dai Yao, and Shen Zimu should have been dismissed but were kept on, contrary to public opinion—and the grand ministers who remain in power, how can they escape responsibility?"

sentences.zh: 無何，劾左都督王之楨久掌錦衣，為內閣爪牙，中樞心腹。

translations.literal: Before long, he impeached Left Chief Commander Wang Zhizhen, who had long controlled the Embroidered Uniform Guard, as a lackey of the Inner Cabinet and a trusted henchman of the central authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, he also impeached Left Chief Commander Wang Zhizhen, who had long headed the Embroidered Uniform Guard, as a lackey of the Inner Cabinet and a trusted henchman at the heart of power.

sentences.zh: 又劾大學士王錫爵逢君賊善，召命宜停；

translations.literal: He further impeached Grand Secretary Wang Xijue for currying favor with the ruler through evil flattery, saying his summons to office should be halted;
translations.idiomatic: He further impeached Grand Secretary Wang Xijue for fawning on the emperor with malicious flattery and urged that his recall to office be stopped;

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書趙世卿誤國，無大臣體。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Zhao Shiqing had harmed the state and lacked the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: He charged that Minister of Revenue Zhao Shiqing had misgoverned the realm and showed none of the dignity expected of a senior minister.

sentences.zh: 已，復言：「朝端大政，宜及今早行者，在放輔臣以清政地，罷大臣被論者以伸公議。

translations.literal: Later he spoke again: "Among great policies at court that ought to be carried out as early as today are dismissing assisting ministers to clear the ground of government, and removing great ministers who had been impeached in order to give scope to public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Later he spoke again: "Among the great matters at court that should be settled at once are dismissing the grand ministers to cleanse the field of government, and removing senior officials who have been impeached so that public opinion may prevail.

sentences.zh: 斥王之楨以絕禍源，釋卞孔時、王邦才等以蘇冤獄。」

translations.literal: Expel Wang Zhizhen to cut off the source of calamity, and release Bian Kongshi, Wang Bangcai, and others to relieve unjust imprisonment."
translations.idiomatic: Drive out Wang Zhizhen to cut off the source of disaster, and release Bian Kongshi, Wang Bangcai, and the others to redress wrongful imprisonment."

sentences.zh: 初，皇長孫生，有詔起廢，列上二百余人。

translations.literal: At first, when the imperial great-grandson was born, an edict was issued to recall the dismissed, and more than two hundred men were listed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the imperial great-grandson was born, an edict was issued to recall dismissed officials, and more than two hundred names were submitted.

sentences.zh: 閱三年，止用顧憲成等四人。

translations.literal: After three years, only four men, including Gu Xancheng, were employed.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, only four men, including Gu Xancheng, had actually been restored to office.

sentences.zh: 士晉請大起廢籍。

translations.literal: Shijin requested a broad recall of those on the rolls of the dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shijin petitioned for a large-scale recall of dismissed officials.

sentences.zh: 瑞王將婚，詔典禮視福王，費當十九萬。

translations.literal: When Prince Rui was about to marry, an edict ordered that ceremonial precedent follow that of Prince Fu, and the expense was set at one hundred ninety thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Rui was about to marry, an edict directed that the ceremonial arrangements follow those of Prince Fu, with costs set at one hundred ninety thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 初，帝弟潞王婚費不及其半，士晉請視潞王。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor's younger brother Prince Lu had married, the expense had not reached half that amount; Shijin requested that Prince Lu's precedent be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor's younger brother Prince Lu had married, the cost had been less than half as much, and Shijin asked that Prince Lu's precedent be followed instead.

sentences.zh: 帝將崇奉太后，詔建靈應宮，士晉以非禮力爭，且曰：「聖母所註念者東宮出講，諸王早婚，與遺賢之登進也，乃諸臣屢請不應。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to honor the empress dowager, and an edict ordered construction of the Lingying Palace; Shijin forcefully contested this as contrary to ritual, saying: "What the Holy Mother cares about is the crown prince leaving the palace to study, the princes marrying early, and worthy men of old being promoted—yet when ministers repeatedly requested these things, there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned to honor the empress dowager and ordered construction of the Lingying Palace, Shijin fought the proposal as improper ritual and said: "What the Holy Mother cares about is the crown prince leaving the palace to study, the early marriages of the princes, and the advancement of worthy men long passed over—yet when ministers repeatedly asked for these things, Your Majesty would not agree.

sentences.zh: 而不時內降者，非中貴之營求，即鬼神之香火，何也？」

translations.literal: Yet what is issued from within the palace from time to time is either the importuning of inner eunuchs or incense offerings to ghosts and spirits—why is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet what issues from the palace from time to time is either something sought by inner eunuchs or offerings to ghosts and spirits—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 帝皆不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took no notice of any of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored it all.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有張差梃擊之事。

translations.literal: Before long, there was the affair of Zhang Chai's club assault.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came the affair of Zhang Chai's club attack.

sentences.zh: 王之寀鉤得差供，帝遷延不決，士晉三上疏趣之。

translations.literal: Wang Zhichai obtained Zhang Chai's confession through investigation, yet the emperor delayed and would not decide; Shijin submitted three memorials urging him on.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhichai obtained Zhang Chai's confession through investigation, yet the emperor kept delaying a decision, and Shijin submitted three memorials urging him to act.

sentences.zh: 當是時，變起非常，中外鹹疑謀出鄭國泰，然無敢直犯其鋒者。

translations.literal: At that time the upheaval was extraordinary; inside and outside the court all suspected the plot came from Zheng Guotai, yet none dared directly to meet his edge.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crisis was extraordinary; court and country alike suspected the plot originated with Zheng Guotai, yet no one dared confront him directly.

sentences.zh: 郎中陸大受稍及之，國泰大懼，急出揭自明，人言益籍籍。

translations.literal: Bureau Director Lu Dashou touched on him slightly; Guotai was greatly afraid and hurriedly issued a public notice to clear himself, and people's talk grew ever more widespread.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Director Lu Dashou touched on him in passing; Guotai was terrified and hurriedly issued a public notice to clear himself, and rumor only spread the more.

sentences.zh: 士晉乃抗疏曰：

translations.literal: Shijin then submitted a forthright memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shijin then submitted a bold memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 陛下與東宮，情親父子，勢共安危，豈有禍逼蕭墻，不少動念者？

translations.literal: Your Majesty and the Eastern Palace are close as father and son in feeling and share fortune and peril in situation—how could calamity press upon the inner courtyard and you remain scarcely moved?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty and the Eastern Palace are bound by the affection of father and son and share a common stake in safety and peril—when disaster threatens the inner court, how can you remain so little moved?

sentences.zh: 候命逾期，旁疑轉棘。

translations.literal: Waiting for orders beyond the deadline, surrounding suspicion grows ever sharper.
translations.idiomatic: As orders are delayed past due time, suspicion all around grows sharper still.

sentences.zh: 竊詳大受之疏，未嘗實指國泰主謀，何張皇自疑乃爾？

translations.literal: I have examined Dashou's memorial in detail: it never actually named Guotai as the chief plotter—why then is he so alarmed and suspicious of himself?
translations.idiomatic: I have read Dashou's memorial carefully: it never actually named Guotai as the chief plotter—so why is he so alarmed and suspicious of himself?

sentences.zh: 因其自疑，人益不能無疑，然人之疑國泰，不自今日始也。

translations.literal: Because he suspects himself, people all the more cannot be without suspicion; yet people's suspicion of Guotai did not begin only today.
translations.idiomatic: Because he suspects himself, others cannot help suspecting him all the more—yet suspicion of Guotai did not begin only today.

sentences.zh: 陛下試問國泰，三王之議何由起？

translations.literal: Your Majesty might ask Guotai: by what means did the debate over the three princes arise?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should ask Guotai: how did the debate over the three princes begin?

sentences.zh: 《閨範》之序何由進？

translations.literal: By what means was the preface to the 《Inner Standards》 submitted?
translations.idiomatic: How did the preface to the 《Inner Standards》 come to be presented?

sentences.zh: 妖書之毒何由構？

translations.literal: By what means was the poison of the demonic book contrived?
translations.idiomatic: How was the poison of the seditious book contrived?

sentences.zh: 此基禍之疑也。

translations.literal: These are the suspicions of laying the foundation of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: These are the suspicions that he laid the groundwork for disaster.

sentences.zh: 孟養浩等何由杖？

translations.literal: By what means were Meng Yanghao and others beaten with rods?
translations.idiomatic: Why were Meng Yanghao and the others beaten with rods?

sentences.zh: 戴士衡等何由戍？

translations.literal: By what means were Dai Shiheng and others sent to frontier garrison duty?
translations.idiomatic: Why were Dai Shiheng and the others banished to frontier garrison duty?

sentences.zh: 王德完等何由錮？

translations.literal: By what means were Wang Dewan and others imprisoned?
translations.idiomatic: Why were Wang Dewan and the others imprisoned?

sentences.zh: 此挑激之疑也。

translations.literal: These are the suspicions of provocation.
translations.idiomatic: These are the suspicions that he stirred up conflict.

sentences.zh: 南宗順，刑余也，而陰募死士千人，謂何？

translations.literal: Nan Zongshun is a castrated man, yet he secretly recruited a thousand death-defying warriors—what does this mean?
translations.idiomatic: Nan Zongshun is a eunuch, yet he secretly recruited a thousand men willing to die for him—what does that mean?

sentences.zh: 順義王，外寇也，而各宮門守以重兵，謂何？

translations.literal: The Prince of Shunyi is a foreign enemy, yet each palace gate is guarded with heavy troops—what does this mean?
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shunyi is a foreign foe, yet every palace gate is held by heavy troops—what does that mean?

sentences.zh: 王曰乾，逆徒也，而疏中先有龐保、劉成名姓，謂何？

translations.literal: Wang Yueqian is a rebel follower, yet in the memorial Pang Bao and Liu Cheng's names appear first—what does this mean?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yueqian is a traitor, yet the memorial names Pang Bao and Liu Cheng first—what does that mean?

sentences.zh: 此不軌之疑也。

translations.literal: These are the suspicions of irregular conduct.
translations.idiomatic: These are the suspicions of treasonous intent.

sentences.zh: 三者積疑至今日，忽有張差一事，正與往者舉措相符，安得令人不疑！

translations.literal: These three kinds of accumulated suspicion reach to today; suddenly there is the affair of Zhang Chai, which exactly matches past actions and measures—how can it not make people suspect!
translations.idiomatic: These three layers of suspicion have built up to today; then suddenly comes the Zhang Chai affair, which fits exactly with past conduct—how can people not suspect!

sentences.zh: 且今日之疑國泰，又非張差一事已也。

translations.literal: Moreover, today's suspicion of Guotai is not exhausted by the affair of Zhang Chai alone.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, suspicion of Guotai today does not rest on the Zhang Chai affair alone.

sentences.zh: 恐騎虎難下，駭鹿走險，一擊不效，別有陰謀。

translations.literal: I fear one rides a tiger and finds it hard to dismount; a startled deer runs into danger; if one strike fails, there will be another hidden plot.
translations.idiomatic: I fear he has mounted a tiger and cannot climb down; like a startled deer he may flee into danger; if one strike fails, another secret plot may follow.

sentences.zh: 陛下不急護東宮，則東宮為孤註。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not urgently protect the Eastern Palace, then the Eastern Palace becomes a lone wager.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not urgently protect the Eastern Palace, the crown prince becomes a lone wager.

sentences.zh: 萬一東宮失護，而陛下又轉為孤註矣。

translations.literal: If by any chance the Eastern Palace loses protection, then Your Majesty in turn becomes a lone wager.
translations.idiomatic: If the Eastern Palace should lose protection, Your Majesty in turn would become the lone wager.

sentences.zh: 國泰欲釋人疑，惟明告貴妃，力求陛下速執保、成下吏。

translations.literal: If Guotai wishes to dispel people's suspicion, he has only to tell the Noble Consort plainly and earnestly urge Your Majesty swiftly to arrest Bao and Cheng and hand them to the law officers.
translations.idiomatic: If Guotai wishes to clear suspicion, he need only tell the Noble Consort plainly and earnestly urge Your Majesty to arrest Bao and Cheng at once and turn them over to the courts.

sentences.zh: 如果國泰主謀，是乾坤之大逆，九廟之罪人，非但貴妃不能庇，即陛下亦不能庇也。

translations.literal: If Guotai was indeed the chief plotter, this is great rebellion against Heaven and Earth and guilt before the Nine Temples; not only the Noble Consort cannot shield him—even Your Majesty cannot shield him.
translations.idiomatic: If Guotai was indeed the chief plotter, that would be treason against Heaven and Earth and guilt before the imperial ancestors; not even the Noble Consort could shield him—and neither could Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 借劍尚方，請自臣始。

translations.literal: To borrow the sword from the imperial workshop, let it begin with your subject.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial sword must be borrowed to punish him, let the blow begin with me.

sentences.zh: 或別有主謀，無與國泰事，請令國泰自任，凡皇太子、皇長孫起居悉屬國泰保護，稍有疏虞，罪即坐之，則臣與在廷諸臣亦願陛下保全國泰身，無替恩禮。

translations.literal: Or if there is another chief plotter and the matter has nothing to do with Guotai, then I ask that Guotai be made personally responsible: all the daily care of the crown prince and the imperial great-grandson shall belong to Guotai's protection; if there is the slightest negligence, let guilt be fixed upon him—then your subject and the ministers at court will also wish Your Majesty to preserve Guotai's person and not diminish his favor and ritual treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Or if another man masterminded the plot and Guotai is innocent, then let Guotai take personal responsibility for the daily care and protection of the crown prince and the imperial great-grandson; if there is the slightest lapse, let him be punished—then I and the ministers at court would also wish Your Majesty to preserve Guotai's person and honor.

sentences.zh: 若國泰畏有連引，預熒惑聖聰，久稽廷訊，或潛散黨與，俾之遠逃，或陰斃張差，以冀滅口，則罪愈不容誅矣。

translations.literal: If Guotai, fearing implication, beforehand confuses the sacred understanding, long delays court interrogation, or secretly disperses his faction so they flee far away, or secretly kills Zhang Chai in hope of silencing him, then his guilt all the more cannot be pardoned by execution.
translations.idiomatic: But if Guotai, fearing implication, seeks beforehand to mislead Your Majesty, long delays court interrogation, secretly disperses his faction so they may flee, or secretly kills Zhang Chai to silence him, then his guilt would be all the less pardonable.

sentences.zh: 惟聖明裁察。

translations.literal: I rely only on sacred clarity to judge and examine.
translations.idiomatic: I leave the matter to Your Majesty's wise judgment.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝大怒，欲罪之，念事已有跡，恐益致人言。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly angered and wished to punish him, but considering that the affair already had traces, he feared this would further provoke talk.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was furious and wished to punish him, but considering that the affair already had visible traces, he feared this would only provoke more talk.

sentences.zh: 而吏部先以士晉為東林黨，擬出為浙江僉事，候命三年未下。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Ministry of Personnel had already classified Shijin as a Donglin partisan and proposed transferring him out as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang; he waited three years and the order did not come down.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Ministry of Personnel had already marked Shijin as a Donglin partisan and proposed transferring him to serve as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang; he waited three years for the appointment order, which never came.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝急簡部疏，命如前擬。

translations.literal: At this point the emperor hurriedly selected the ministry's memorial and ordered as previously proposed.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the emperor hurriedly picked out the ministry's proposal and ordered that it be carried out as previously recommended.

sentences.zh: 吏部言闕官已補，請改命。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel said the vacant post had already been filled and requested a changed appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel replied that the vacant post had already been filled and asked that a new appointment be made.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，命調前補者。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit this and ordered the earlier appointee transferred.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and ordered the man previously appointed to be transferred elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 吏部又以士晉積資已深，秩當參議。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel also argued that Shijin's accumulated seniority was already deep and his rank ought to be Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel also argued that Shijin's accumulated seniority already qualified him for the rank of Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，切責尚書，奪郎中以下俸。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, sharply rebuked the minister, and stripped the salaries of those below bureau directors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, sharply rebuked the minister, and docked the salaries of officials below the rank of bureau director.

sentences.zh: 士晉之官四年，移廣西參議。

translations.literal: Shijin took office for four years and was transferred to Administration Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shijin served four years in that post before being transferred to Administration Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，擢尚寶少卿，遷太仆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Treasures and transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, Shijin was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Treasures and then transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，以右僉都御史巡撫廣西。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tianqi reign he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 安南入犯，督將吏屢擊卻之。

translations.literal: When Annam invaded, he supervised generals and officials and repeatedly struck and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: When Annam invaded, he directed the generals and officials and repeatedly drove the invaders back.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢兵部右侍郎，總督兩廣軍務，兼巡撫廣東。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War, Supreme Commander of military affairs in the Two Guangs, and concurrently Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War, made Supreme Commander of military affairs in the Two Guangs, and concurrently appointed Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，魏忠賢大熾，爭梃擊者率獲罪。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year Wei Zhongxian was greatly ascendant, and those who had contested the club assault mostly met punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year Wei Zhongxian was at the height of his power, and those who had challenged the official account of the club assault were mostly punished.

sentences.zh: 御史田景新希旨，誣叛臣安邦彥賄士晉十萬金，阻援兵。

translations.literal: Censor Tian Jingxin, seeking to please higher intent, falsely charged that the rebel minister An Bangyan had bribed Shijin with one hundred thousand in gold to obstruct relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tian Jingxin, eager to please his superiors, falsely charged that the rebel An Bangyan had bribed Shijin with one hundred thousand taels of gold to block relief troops.

sentences.zh: 遂除士晉名，征賄助餉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shijin's name was removed from office and he was charged with taking bribes to aid military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Shijin was then dismissed from office and charged with taking bribes to aid military supplies.

sentences.zh: 士晉憤郁而卒。

translations.literal: Shijin died in indignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: Shijin died of indignant grief.

sentences.zh: 有司征贓急，家人但輸數百金，產已罄。

translations.literal: The authorities urgently demanded restitution of illicit gains; the family could pay only several hundred in gold, and their property was already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities urgently demanded restitution of illicit gains; the family could pay only a few hundred taels, for their property was already exhausted.

sentences.zh: 會莊烈帝立，獲免，復官賜恤。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended, he was pardoned, restored to office, and granted posthumous consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne, Shijin was pardoned, his office restored, and posthumous honors granted.

sentences.zh: 陸大受，字凝遠，武進人。

translations.literal: Lu Dashou, style name Ningyuan, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dashou, styled Ningyuan, was a native of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirty-fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-fifth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人，屢遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier and was repeatedly promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed courier and was promoted in stages to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 福王將之國，詔賜莊田四萬頃。

translations.literal: When Prince Fu was about to go to his fief, an edict granted him forty thousand qing of estate lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Fu was about to depart for his fief, an edict granted him forty thousand qing of estate lands.

sentences.zh: 大受請大減田額，因劾鄭國泰驕恣亂法狀，疏留中。

translations.literal: Dashou requested a great reduction in the land quota and thereby impeached Zheng Guotai's arrogant, willful, law-disturbing conduct; the memorial was kept within.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou asked for a large reduction in the land grant and impeached Zheng Guotai for arrogant lawlessness; the memorial was kept within the palace and never answered.

sentences.zh: 王之寀發張差事，大受抗疏言：「青宮何地，張差何人，敢白晝持梃，直犯儲蹕，此乾坤何等時耶！

translations.literal: When Wang Zhichai exposed the Zhang Chai affair, Dashou submitted a forthright memorial saying: "What place is the Eastern Palace? Who is Zhang Chai, that he dares in broad daylight to wield a club and directly violate the heir's resting place—what sort of time is this for Heaven and Earth!
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhichai exposed the Zhang Chai affair, Dashou submitted a bold memorial saying: "What place is the Eastern Palace? Who is Zhang Chai, that he dares in broad daylight to wield a club and strike at the heir apparent's residence—what age is this for Heaven and Earth!

sentences.zh: 業承一內官，何以不知其名？

translations.literal: He had served one inner eunuch—how could his name not be known?
translations.idiomatic: He had served an inner eunuch—how can his name still be unknown?

sentences.zh: 業承一大第，何以不知其所？

translations.literal: He had served one great mansion—how could its location not be known?
translations.idiomatic: He had served at a great mansion—how can its location still be unknown?

sentences.zh: 彼三老、三太互相表裏，而霸州武舉高順寧者，今皆匿於何地？

translations.literal: Those three elders and three grandees mutually shield one another inside and out, and Gao Shunning of Bazhou, a military licentiate—where are they all hidden now?
translations.idiomatic: The three elders and three grandees shield one another, and Gao Shunning of Bazhou, a military licentiate—where are they all hiding now?

sentences.zh: 奈何不嚴竟而速斷耶？」

translations.literal: Why not thoroughly investigate instead of cutting the case short so quickly?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not investigate thoroughly instead of closing the case so hastily?"

sentences.zh: 戶部主事蒲州張庭者，大受同年生也，亦上言：「奸人突入大內，狙擊青宮，陛下宜何如震怒，立窮主謀。

translations.literal: Section Chief Zhang Ting of Puzhou in the Ministry of Revenue was Dashou's fellow graduate of the same year; he also submitted a statement: "Evil men burst into the inner palace and ambushed the Eastern Palace—how ought Your Majesty to be shaken with anger and at once exhaustively pursue the chief plot?
translations.idiomatic: Section Chief Zhang Ting of Puzhou in the Ministry of Revenue, a fellow jinshi of Dashou's year, also submitted a memorial: "Wicked men broke into the inner palace and attacked the Eastern Palace—Your Majesty ought to be shaken with rage and immediately pursue the chief plot to the end.

sentences.zh: 乃廷臣交章，一無批答，何也？

translations.literal: Yet court ministers submitted memorial after memorial and received not one written reply—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet court ministers submitted memorial after memorial and received not a single written reply—why?

sentences.zh: 君側藏奸，上下蒙蔽，皆由陛下精神偏註，皇太子召見甚稀，而前此冊立、選婚及近時東宮出講、郭妃卜葬諸事，陛下皆弗勝遲回，強而後可。

translations.literal: Evil hidden at the ruler's side and deception above and below all stem from Your Majesty's attention being narrowly fixed; the crown prince is summoned to audience very rarely, and earlier the investiture, the selection of a consort, and recently the Eastern Palace leaving to study, the divination of burial for Consort Guo, and other matters—all these Your Majesty could not but delay and hesitate over, yielding only after being pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Evil hidden at the ruler's side and deception throughout the court all stem from Your Majesty's divided attention; the crown prince is rarely summoned to audience, and whether in the earlier investiture and selection of a consort or in recent matters such as the crown prince leaving the palace to study and the divination of burial for Consort Guo, Your Majesty has always hesitated and yielded only when pressed.

sentences.zh: 彼宦寺者安得不妄生測度，陰蓄不逞，以僥幸於萬一哉！」

translations.literal: How could those palace eunuchs fail to recklessly form conjectures, secretly harbor discontent, and gamble on a one-in-ten-thousand chance!"
translations.idiomatic: How could palace eunuchs fail to indulge wild suspicions, secretly harbor disloyal designs, and gamble on a chance in ten thousand!"

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: None of these memorials received any reply.

sentences.zh: 大受尋出為撫州知府，以清潔著聞。

translations.literal: Dashou was soon sent out as prefect of Fuzhou and became known for integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou was soon sent out to serve as prefect of Fuzhou, where he became known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 居二年，徐紹吉、韓浚以京察奪其官。

translations.literal: After two years Xu Shaoji and Han Jun stripped him of office through the capital evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: After two years Xu Shaoji and Han Jun stripped him of office in the capital evaluation.

sentences.zh: 庭再遷郎中，被齮龁。

translations.literal: Ting was again promoted to bureau director and was gnawed at by slander.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was promoted again to bureau director but was hounded by slander.

sentences.zh: 引退，抑郁以死。

translations.literal: He withdrew and died in depression.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew from office and died in depression.

sentences.zh: 又有聞喜李俸者，為刑部郎中。

translations.literal: There was also Li Feng of Wenxi, serving as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Another was Li Feng of Wenxi, who served as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 當諸司會鞫時，張差語涉逆謀，郎中胡士相等相顧不敢錄。

translations.literal: When the various offices jointly interrogated, Zhang Chai's words touched on treasonous plotting; Bureau Director Hu Shixiang and others looked at one another and dared not record them.
translations.idiomatic: When the various offices jointly interrogated the case, Zhang Chai's testimony touched on treason; Bureau Director Hu Shixiang and the others exchanged glances and dared not record it.

sentences.zh: 俸力爭，乃得入獄詞，遂為鄭氏黨所惡。

translations.literal: Feng forcefully contended and only then got the confession entered into the record; he was thereupon hated by the Zheng faction.
translations.idiomatic: Feng argued forcefully until the confession was entered into the record, and was thereafter hated by the Zheng faction.

sentences.zh: 及遷鳳翔知府，諸黨人以言懾之，竟不敢之任。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to prefect of Fengxiang, the faction members intimidated him with words, and in the end he did not dare take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to serve as prefect of Fengxiang, the faction intimidated him with threats, and in the end he did not dare take up the post.

sentences.zh: 後復中以京察，卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he was again dismissed in the capital evaluation and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed again in the capital evaluation and died at home.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，御史張慎言、方震孺、魏光緒、楊新期交章訟三人冤。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, Censors Zhang Shenyan, Fang Zhenru, Wei Guangxu, and Yang Xinqi submitted memorials in succession pleading the innocence of the three men.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, Censors Zhang Shenyan, Fang Zhenru, Wei Guangxu, and Yang Xinqi submitted memorial after memorial pleading the innocence of the three men.

sentences.zh: 乃贈庭、俸光祿寺少卿，大受起補韶州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ting and Feng were posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Dashou was recalled to fill the post at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ting and Feng were then posthumously granted the title of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Dashou was recalled to serve at Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 已，都御史高攀龍請加庭、俸蔭謚，不果。

translations.literal: Later Censor-in-Chief Gao Panlong requested added hereditary privilege and posthumous titles for Ting and Feng, but this did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Censor-in-Chief Gao Panlong asked that additional hereditary privileges and posthumous titles be granted to Ting and Feng, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 大受未幾卒。

translations.literal: Dashou died before long.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 王德完，字子醇，廣安人。

translations.literal: Wang Dewan, style name Zichun, was a native of Guang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dewan, styled Zichun, was a native of Guang'an.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fourteenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，改兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and was transferred to supervising secretary of the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and was transferred to supervising secretary in the military section.

sentences.zh: 西陲失事，德完言：「諸邊歲糜餉數百萬，而士氣日衰，戎備日廢者，以三蠹未除，二策未審也。

translations.literal: When the western frontier suffered setbacks, Dewan said: "The borders each year consume supplies of several million, yet morale daily declines and military readiness daily decays because three pests have not been removed and two policies have not been examined.
translations.idiomatic: When the western frontier suffered setbacks, Dewan said: "The borders consume millions in supplies each year, yet morale keeps falling and defenses keep decaying because three corruptions have not been removed and two policies have not been settled.

sentences.zh: 何為三蠹？

translations.literal: What are the three pests?
translations.idiomatic: What are the three corruptions?

sentences.zh: 一曰欺，邊吏罔上也。

translations.literal: The first is called deception: frontier officials deceive those above them.
translations.idiomatic: The first is deception—frontier officials lying to their superiors.

sentences.zh: 二曰徇，市賞增額也。

translations.literal: The second is partiality: selling rewards and increasing quotas.
translations.idiomatic: The second is favoritism: inflating rewards and quotas for sale.

sentences.zh: 三曰虛，邊防鮮實也。

translations.literal: The third is emptiness: frontier defenses rarely have substance.
translations.idiomatic: The third is hollowness: frontier defenses exist mostly on paper.

sentences.zh: 何謂二策？

translations.literal: What are called the two policies?
translations.idiomatic: What do these two policies mean?

sentences.zh: 有目前之策，有經久之策。

translations.literal: There is a policy for the present moment; there is a policy for lasting permanence.
translations.idiomatic: One policy addresses the immediate crisis; the other is meant to endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 謹守誓盟，茍免搏噬，此計在目前。

translations.literal: Strictly maintaining sworn alliances, barely escaping mutual tearing and biting—this plan belongs to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Clinging to sworn treaties just to ward off open conflict—that is the short-term approach.

sentences.zh: 大修戰具，令賊不敢窺邊，則百年可保無事，此計在經久。

translations.literal: Greatly repairing war equipment, causing the bandits not to dare peep at the border, then a hundred years may be kept without incident—this plan lies in lasting permanence.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuilding the arsenal in earnest so that enemies dare not even glance at the frontier—then peace might hold for a century. That is the long-term plan.

sentences.zh: 今經略鄭洛主款，巡撫葉夢熊又言戰，邊臣不協，安望成功。」

translations.literal: Now the frontier commissioner Zheng Luo advocates peace, yet the grand coordinator Ye Mengxiong again speaks of war—the border officials are not in accord; how can one hope for success?
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commissioner Zheng Luo argued for reconciliation while the grand coordinator Ye Mengxiong pressed for war. With the border commanders at odds, what hope was there of success?"

sentences.zh: 帝為飭二臣。

translations.literal: [Close quote] The Emperor therefore rebuked the two officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon upbraided both men.

sentences.zh: 石星為本兵，德完上十議以規時，帝納之。

translations.literal: Shi Xing served as Minister of War; Dewan submitted ten proposals to assess the times, and the Emperor accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Xing as Minister of War, Dewan memorialized ten proposals on the state of affairs, and the Emperor approved them.

sentences.zh: 已，請裁李成梁父子權，劾褫黔國公沐昌祚冠服，罷巡撫朱孟震、賈待問、郭四維、少卿楊四知、趙卿。

translations.literal: Soon after, he requested curbing the authority of Li Chengliang and his son, impeached and stripped the Duke of Qian Mu Changzuo of cap and robes, and dismissed the grand coordinators Zhu Mengzhen, Jia Daiwen, and Guo Siwei, and Vice Ministers Yang Sizhi and Zhao Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged that the powers of Li Chengliang and his son be reduced; called for stripping the Duke of Qian, Mu Changzuo, of his rank and regalia; and demanded the dismissal of the grand coordinators Zhu Mengzhen, Jia Daiwen, and Guo Siwei, together with Vice Ministers Yang Sizhi and Zhao Qing.

sentences.zh: 又發廣東總督劉繼文、總兵官李棟等冒功罪。

translations.literal: He further exposed the crime of Guangdong Governor-General Liu Jiwen, Commander-in-Chief Li Dong, and others for falsely claiming merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also charged Guangdong Governor-General Liu Jiwen, Commander Li Dong, and others with fabricating military laurels.

sentences.zh: 半歲章數十上，率軍國大計。

translations.literal: Within half a year he submitted memorials numbering several tens; mostly they concerned the great plans of army and state.
translations.idiomatic: In six months he filed dozens of memorials, nearly all on matters vital to the army and the realm.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to supervising secretary of the Household Section.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to become supervising secretary of the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 上籌畫邊餉議，言：「諸邊歲例，弘、正間止四十三萬，至嘉靖則二百七十余萬，而今則三百八十余萬。

translations.literal: He submitted a plan for border rations, saying: "The annual allotments for the frontiers, between the Hongzhi and Zhengde reigns, amounted to only 430,000; by the Jiajing era they reached over 2,700,000; and now they exceed 3,800,000.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on frontier supplies, observing: "Annual border allotments totaled a mere 430,000 taels in the Hongzhi and Zhengde periods, rose to more than 2,700,000 under Jiajing, and now stand above 3,800,000.

sentences.zh: 惟力行節儉，足以補救。

translations.literal: Only by vigorously practicing thrift can one suffice to remedy this.
translations.idiomatic: Only resolute austerity can make up the gap.

sentences.zh: 蓋耗蠹之弊，外易剔而內難除。

translations.literal: For the evil of waste and corruption, what lies without is easy to prune away, but what lies within is hard to remove.
translations.idiomatic: Outward waste can be trimmed away; corruption rooted inside the palace is far harder to purge.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴劾內府諸庫，汰其不急。

translations.literal: One ought strictly to impeach the inner palace treasuries and eliminate what is not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The inner treasuries should be rigorously audited and every nonessential expense cut.

sentences.zh: 又加意屯田、鹽法，外開其源，而內節其流，庶幾國用可足。」

translations.literal: Moreover, give added attention to garrison farming and the salt monopoly: open the source without, and economize the flow within—then perhaps state revenue may suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Revive garrison farming and reform the salt tax—expand income abroad while tightening expenditure at court—and the treasury might once again be sound."

sentences.zh: 時弗能用。

translations.literal: [Close quote] At the time his advice could not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: His proposals went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 倭寇久躪朝鮮，再議封貢。

translations.literal: Japanese bandits long trampled Korea; enfeoffment and tribute were debated again.
translations.idiomatic: With Japanese raiders ravaging Korea for years, the court once again debated granting enfeoffment and accepting tribute.

sentences.zh: 德完言：「封則必貢，貢則必市，是沈惟敬誤經略，經略誤總督，總督誤本兵，本兵誤朝廷也。」

translations.literal: Dewan said: "Enfeoffment necessarily entails tribute; tribute necessarily entails trade. Thus Shen Weijing misled the frontier commissioner, the frontier commissioner misled the governor-general, the governor-general misled the Minister of War, and the Minister of War misled the court.
translations.idiomatic: Dewan warned: "Grant enfeoffment and tribute must follow; allow tribute and trade will follow. Shen Weijing led the frontier commissioner astray, the commissioner led the governor-general astray, the governor-general led the Minister of War astray, and the Minister of War led the entire court astray."

sentences.zh: 後封果不成。

translations.literal: [Close quote] Later, enfeoffment indeed did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, enfeoffment failed exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 德完尋以疾歸。

translations.literal: Before long Dewan returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Dewan soon retired, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，起任工科。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was recalled to serve in the Works Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of the reign he was recalled to a post in the Works Section.

sentences.zh: 極陳四川采木、榷稅及播州用兵之患。

translations.literal: He exhaustively set forth the evils of timber-cutting in Sichuan, monopoly taxation, and the use of troops in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out at length the disasters of Sichuan timber levies, excise taxes, and the Bozhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 又言三殿未營，不宜復興玄殿、龍舟之役。

translations.literal: He further said that since the three main halls had not yet been built, it was unfitting to revive projects for the Mystic Hall and the dragon barges.
translations.idiomatic: He added that with the three main halls still unfinished, the court ought not revive work on the Mystic Hall and the imperial dragon barges.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered none of these memorials.

sentences.zh: 已，劾湖廣稅使陳奉四大罪。

translations.literal: Soon after, he impeached Chen Feng, the tax commissioner of Huguang, on four great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Chen Feng, the Huguang tax commissioner, on four major counts.

sentences.zh: 再疏極論，謂奉必激變。

translations.literal: In a second memorial he argued to the utmost, saying Feng would surely provoke rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: A second memorial argued forcefully that Chen Feng was bound to provoke a revolt.

sentences.zh: 奉果為楚人所攻，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Feng was indeed attacked by men of Chu and barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Feng was indeed set upon by the people of Chu and escaped with his life only by flight.

sentences.zh: 尋因禱雨言：「今出虎兕以噬群黎，縱盜賊而吞赤子，幽憤沈結，叩訴無從，故雨澤緣天怒而屯，螟丱因人妖而出。

translations.literal: Soon, on the occasion of praying for rain, he said: "Now tigers and rhinoceroses are released to devour the common people; bandits are left loose to swallow infants. Deep grievances sink and knot; there is no way to knock and plead. Hence rain delays because Heaven is angry, and crop pests appear because human anomalies arise.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, in a rain-prayer memorial, he wrote: "The court sends out tigers to prey on the people and unleashes bandits to devour the innocent. Grievances fester with nowhere to turn for redress, so rain withholds itself in Heaven's wrath and locusts swarm because the realm has gone wrong.

sentences.zh: 願盡撤礦稅之使，釋逮系之臣，省愆贖過，用弭災變。」

translations.literal: I wish to withdraw entirely the mining-tax envoys, release imprisoned officials, examine faults and redeem transgressions, thereby to quell calamity and anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw every mining-tax envoy, free the officials in prison, repent and make amends—and perhaps the heavens' warning might be stilled."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: [Close quote] No reply.
translations.idiomatic: No response came.

sentences.zh: 四川妖人韓應龍奏請榷鹽、采木。

translations.literal: Han Yinglong, a sorcerer of Sichuan, memorialized requesting salt monopoly and timber-cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yinglong, a Sichuan sorcerer, petitioned to levy salt taxes and harvest timber.

sentences.zh: 尋甸知府蔡如川、趙州知州甘學書以忤稅使被逮。

translations.literal: Cai Ruchuan, prefect of Xundian, and Gan Xueshu, magistrate of Zhaozhou, were arrested for offending the tax commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ruchuan, prefect of Xundian, and Gan Xueshu, magistrate of Zhaozhou, were arrested for defying the tax envoys.

sentences.zh: 德完皆力爭。

translations.literal: Dewan in every case strove forcefully against this.
translations.idiomatic: Dewan fought each case vigorously.

sentences.zh: 復劾山東稅使陳增、畿輔稅使王虎罪。

translations.literal: He again impeached Chen Zeng, tax commissioner of Shandong, and Wang Hu, tax commissioner of the capital region, for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He again impeached the Shandong tax commissioner Chen Zeng and the metropolitan tax commissioner Wang Hu.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply.
translations.idiomatic: Again there was no response.

sentences.zh: 已極陳國計匱乏，言：「近歲寧夏用兵，費百八十余萬；

translations.literal: Soon he exhaustively set forth the depletion of state finances, saying: "In recent years the campaign in Ningxia cost more than 1,800,000;
translations.idiomatic: He next laid bare the treasury's exhaustion: "The Ningxia campaign alone in recent years has cost more than 1,800,000 taels;

sentences.zh: 朝鮮之役，七百八十余萬；

translations.literal: The Korean expedition, more than 7,800,000;
translations.idiomatic: the Korean war over 7,800,000;

sentences.zh: 播州之役，二百余萬。

translations.literal: The Bozhou campaign, more than 2,000,000.
translations.idiomatic: the Bozhou campaign more than 2,000,000.

sentences.zh: 今皇長子及諸王子冊封、冠婚至九百三十四萬，而袍服之費復二百七十余萬，冗費如此，國何以支？」

translations.literal: Now the investiture, enfeoffment, capping, and marriage of the heir apparent and the various princes reach 9,340,000, while the cost of robes and garments again exceeds 2,700,000—extravagance such as this, how can the state be sustained?
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffment, investiture, and wedding ceremonies for the heir apparent and the princes now total 9,340,000 taels, with robe and garment costs adding another 2,700,000. With waste on this scale, how can the treasury endure?"

sentences.zh: 因請減織造，止營建，亟完殿工，停買珠寶，慎重采辦，大發內帑，語極切至。

translations.literal: [Close quote] He thereupon requested reducing textile manufacture, halting construction projects, urgently completing the hall works, stopping the purchase of pearls and gems, treating procurement with care, and greatly releasing funds from the inner treasury—his words were extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded to cut textile orders, halt new construction, finish the hall project quickly, stop buying jewels, review procurement carefully, and draw heavily on the inner treasury—every word spoken with urgent sincerity.

sentences.zh: 帝亦不省。

translations.literal: The Emperor also did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 時帝寵鄭貴妃，疏皇后及皇長子。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor favored Lady Zheng, the Noble Consort, and kept distant from the Empress and the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor doted on Noble Consort Zheng while neglecting the Empress and the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 皇長子生母王恭妃幾殆，而皇后亦多疾。

translations.literal: The birth mother of the heir apparent, Lady Wang the Respectful Consort, nearly perished, and the Empress also suffered many illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's mother, Lady Wang, barely survived, and the Empress herself fell frequently ill.

sentences.zh: 左右多竊意後崩，貴妃即正中宮位，其子為太子。

translations.literal: Those around the throne mostly privately supposed that once the Empress died, the Noble Consort would at once occupy the central palace position and her son would become heir.
translations.idiomatic: Court insiders whispered that when the Empress died, Noble Consort Zheng would take her place and make her son crown prince.

sentences.zh: 中允黃輝，皇長子講官也，從內侍微探得其狀，謂德完曰：「此國家大事，旦夕不測，書之史冊，謂朝廷無人。」

translations.literal: Huang Hui, an assistant in the Academy and lecturer to the heir apparent, subtly inquired through inner eunuchs and learned the situation. He said to Dewan: "This is a great matter of state; disaster may come at any hour. If it is written in the chronicles that the court had no men.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui, the heir apparent's tutor, learned the situation through discreet inquiries among palace eunuchs and told Dewan: "This strikes at the heart of the realm. Disaster may come at any hour, and history will record that the court had no men worth the name."

sentences.zh: 德完乃屬輝具草。

translations.literal: [Close quote] Dewan then had Hui prepare the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Dewan asked Huang Hui to draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 十月，上疏言：「道路喧傳，謂中宮役使僅數人，伊郁致疾，阽危弗自保，臣不勝驚疑。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he submitted a memorial, saying: "On the roads there is clamorous rumor that the Central Palace has only a few attendants, that repressed gloom has brought illness, that she stands on the brink and cannot preserve herself—I cannot overcome my shock and doubt.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he memorialized: "Rumors run wild that the Empress has been left with only a handful of servants, that despair has brought her to illness and the edge of death. I am shaken and cannot banish my doubts.

sentences.zh: 宮禁嚴秘，虛實未審。

translations.literal: The palace prohibition is strict and secret; truth and falsehood cannot yet be verified.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace is sealed tight; I cannot know what is true.

sentences.zh: 臣即愚昧，決知其不然。

translations.literal: Though I am foolish, I am resolved that it cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: For all my dullness, I refuse to believe it.

sentences.zh: 第臺諫之官得風聞言事。

translations.literal: Only that officials of the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau may speak on matters heard by rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet censors and remonstrators are permitted to speak on hearsay.

sentences.zh: 果中宮不得於陛下以致疾與？

translations.literal: If it is true that the Central Palace has not found favor with Your Majesty and thus fell ill—is it so?
translations.idiomatic: If the Empress has lost Your Majesty's favor and sickened because of it—

sentences.zh: 則子於父母之怒，當號泣幾諫。

translations.literal: Then, as a child before a parent's anger, one ought to wail and nearly remonstrate to death.
translations.idiomatic: then as a filial son before an angry parent, I should weep and remonstrate without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 果陛下眷遇中宮有加無替歟？

translations.literal: If it is true that Your Majesty's gracious regard for the Central Palace grows without end—is it so?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's affection for the Empress truly grows without end, is that so?

sentences.zh: 則子於父母之謗，當昭雪辨明。

translations.literal: Then, as a child before a parent's slander, one ought to clarify and vindicate.
translations.idiomatic: Then, as a filial son hearing his parents slandered, I should speak up to clear their name.

sentences.zh: 衡是兩端，皆難緘默。

translations.literal: Weighing these two extremes, in both it is hard to remain silent.
translations.idiomatic: Either way, silence is impossible.

sentences.zh: 敢效漢朝袁盎卻坐之議，陳其愚誠。」

translations.literal: I dare emulate Yuan Ang's "please be seated" proposal of the Han dynasty and set forth my foolish sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to follow Yuan Ang of Han, who dared remonstrate even over where the Empress Dowager should sit, and offer my humble counsel."

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝震怒，立下詔獄拷訊。

translations.literal: [Close quote] When the memorial entered, the Emperor was greatly enraged and immediately placed him in the imperial prison for interrogation under torture.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial enraged the Emperor, who had Dewan thrown into the imperial prison for interrogation under torture.

sentences.zh: 尚書李戴、御史周盤等連疏論救。

translations.literal: Minister Li Dai, Censor Zhou Pan, and others submitted memorials in succession to argue for his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Dai, Censor Zhou Pan, and others filed one memorial after another in his defense.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，切責，御史奪俸有差。

translations.literal: Defying the imperial will, they were sharply rebuked; the censors had their salaries reduced in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Their appeals defied the throne; the Emperor rebuked them harshly and docked the censors' salaries by varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫力疾草奏為德完解，帝亦不釋。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan, straining against illness, drafted a memorial to exonerate Dewan, yet the Emperor still did not release him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan, though gravely ill, drafted a plea on Dewan's behalf—but the Emperor would not relent.

sentences.zh: 旋廷杖百，除其名。

translations.literal: Shortly he received a hundred blows in court and was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Dewan was soon beaten a hundred strokes at court and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 復傳諭廷臣：「諸臣為皇長子耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent word instructing the court officials: "Do you act for the heir apparent?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then sent word to the court: "Are you pleading for the heir apparent?

sentences.zh: 抑為德完耶？

translations.literal: Or do you act for Dewan?
translations.idiomatic: Or for Dewan?

sentences.zh: 如為皇長子，慎無擾瀆。

translations.literal: If for the heir apparent, take care not to disturb and offend.
translations.idiomatic: If for the heir apparent, do not vex and trouble him further.

sentences.zh: 必欲為德完，則再遲冊立一歲。」

translations.literal: If you must act for Dewan, then the investiture as heir will again be delayed one year.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on defending Dewan, I shall delay the heir's investiture yet another year."

sentences.zh: 廷臣乃不復言。

translations.literal: [Close quote] The court officials then spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: The officials fell silent.

sentences.zh: 然帝自是懼外廷議論，眷禮中宮，始終無間矣。

translations.literal: Yet from this the Emperor feared outside-court discussion; his gracious care for the Central Palace from beginning to end knew no break.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Emperor feared open debate at court and treated the Empress with unbroken regard.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，召為太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended, he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, Dewan was recalled as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 俄擢左僉都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，京師獲間諜，詞連司禮中官盧受。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, a spy was captured in the capital; the case implicated the eunuch Lu Shou of the Directorate of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi a spy was seized in the capital, and the investigation implicated Lu Shou, a eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 德完請出受南京。

translations.literal: Dewan requested that Shou be dispatched to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Dewan asked that Lu Shou be sent to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 初，德完直聲震天下。

translations.literal: At first, Dewan's reputation for integrity shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In his early years Dewan's moral courage was famed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 及居大僚，持論每與鄒元標等異。

translations.literal: When he rose to high office, his positions often differed from those of Zou Yuanbiao and others.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached high office, his views often diverged from those of Zou Yuanbiao and his allies.

sentences.zh: 楊鎬、李如楨喪師論死，廷臣急欲誅之。

translations.literal: Yang Hao and Li Ruzhen, having lost their armies, were judged worthy of death; the court officials urgently wished to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hao and Li Ruzhen faced execution for losing their armies, and the court clamored for their heads.

sentences.zh: 德完乃上疏請酌公論，或遣戍立功，或即時正辟，蓋設兩途以俟帝寬之。

translations.literal: Dewan then submitted a memorial requesting weighing public opinion: either send them to the frontier to earn merit through service, or immediately apply lawful execution—setting up two paths in hope the Emperor would show leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Dewan memorialized that public opinion be weighed: exile them to the frontier to redeem themselves in battle, or execute them at once—offering both options so the Emperor might show mercy.

sentences.zh: 且因薦順天府丞邵輔忠、通政參議吳殿邦，以兩人嘗力攻李三才也。

translations.literal: Moreover he recommended Shao Fuzhong, vice prefect of Shuntian, and Wu Dianbang, vice director of the Office of Transmission, because the two men had once forcefully attacked Li Sancai.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Shao Fuzhong of Shuntian and Wu Dianbang of the Office of Transmission—both men who had fiercely opposed Li Sancai.

sentences.zh: 疏出，果寬鎬等。

translations.literal: When the memorial appeared, Hao and the others were indeed treated leniently.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was acted upon, and Yang Hao and the others were spared.

sentences.zh: 於是給事中魏大中再疏論之，德完亦力辨。

translations.literal: Thereupon the supervising secretary Wei Dazhong again memorialized on the matter, and Dewan also argued forcefully in his own defense.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wei Dazhong protested in a fresh memorial, and Dewan defended himself vigorously.

sentences.zh: 帝為詰責大中，事乃已。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon rebuked and interrogated Dazhong, and the matter then ended.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor upbraided Wei Dazhong, and the affair subsided.

sentences.zh: 德完尋進戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Dewan was soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Dewan was soon made Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 給事中朱欽相、倪思輝言事獲罪，疏救之。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Zhu Qinxiang and Ni Sihui were punished for speaking on affairs; he memorialized to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: When supervising secretaries Zhu Qinxiang and Ni Sihui were punished for remonstrating, he petitioned for their release.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷左。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to the left [vice ministership].
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to the left vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 亡何卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 其後輔忠、殿邦以黨逆敗，僉為德完惜之。

translations.literal: Afterward Fuzhong and Dianbang fell on charges of faction and treason; all pitied Dewan for this.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shao Fuzhong and Wu Dianbang were ruined in factional treason cases, and many lamented Dewan's poor judgment in recommending them.

sentences.zh: 蔣允儀，字聞韶，宜興人。

translations.literal: Jiang Yunyi, styled Wenshao, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yunyi, courtesy name Wenshao, came from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a presented scholar in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授桐鄉知縣，移嘉興。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Tongxiang and was transferred to Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Tongxiang before being transferred to Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，擢御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was elevated to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 時廣寧已失，熊廷弼、王化貞俱論死，而兵部尚書張鶴鳴如故，糾之者反獲譴。

translations.literal: At the time Guangning had already been lost; Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen were both judged worthy of death, yet Minister of War Zhang Heming remained as before, while those who impeached him in turn received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Guangning had fallen; Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen faced execution—yet Minister of War Zhang Heming kept his post while those who impeached him were themselves punished.

sentences.zh: 允儀不平，疏詆其同罪佚罰。

translations.literal: Yunyi was indignant and submitted a memorial denouncing Heming for sharing guilt yet escaping punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Outraged, Yunyi memorialized that Zhang Heming shared their guilt yet escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 因言：「近言官稍進苦口，輒見齟齬，遷謫未已，申之戒諭。

translations.literal: He further said: "Recently, when censors offer even a little bitter counsel, they immediately meet friction; transfers and demotions have not ceased, followed by admonitions and instructions.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Lately whenever a censor dares speak plainly, he meets immediate resistance—demotions and transfers without end, capped by imperial admonition.

sentences.zh: 使諸臣不遵明諭，而引裾折檻以甘斥逐，天下事猶可為也；

translations.literal: If the various officials do not follow the clear instructions but instead pull the robe and break the balustrade, gladly accepting dismissal—affairs under Heaven could still be managed;
translations.idiomatic: If officials defied those admonitions and, like Zhu Yun clutching the emperor's robe and breaking the balustrade, welcomed exile for honest speech—there would still be hope for the realm;

sentences.zh: 使諸臣果遵明諭，而箝口結舌以保祿位，天下事尚忍言哉！

translations.literal: If the various officials truly follow the clear instructions and seal their mouths and tie their tongues to preserve salary and rank—affairs under Heaven, how can one bear to speak!
translations.idiomatic: But if officials obey and hold their tongues to keep their posts—then who can bear to speak of the fate of the empire!

sentences.zh: 頃者恒旸不雨，二麥無秋，皇上於宮中祈禱，反得冰雹之災。

translations.literal: Recently there has been constant sunshine without rain; the two wheat crops had no harvest. The Emperor prayed within the palace and instead received the calamity of hail.
translations.idiomatic: Drought has lingered without rain; the wheat crop failed. The Emperor prayed within the palace—and hail fell instead.

sentences.zh: 變不虛生，各以類應。

translations.literal: Anomalies do not arise without cause; each responds according to its kind.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warnings are never empty; each omen answers its cause.

sentences.zh: 夫以坤維之厚重而震撼於妖孽，以胡眉之丈夫而交關於婦寺，以籍叢煬竈之奸而托之奉公潔己，是皆陰脅陽之徵也。」

translations.literal: For the heavy substantiality of earth's dimension to be shaken by demons and monsters; for thick-browed men to traffic with women and eunuchs; for wicked men of bramble thickets and kitchen hearths to cloak themselves in serving the public and keeping themselves pure—these are all signs of yin coercing yang.
translations.idiomatic: When the solid earth itself quakes before sorcery, when bold men consort with women and eunuchs, when lowborn villains pose as selfless servants of the state—these are all omens of yin overwhelming yang."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: [Close quote] Acknowledgment was reported.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was noted and filed.

sentences.zh: 鶴鳴既屢被劾，因詆劾者為群奸朋謀，而反與前尚書黃嘉善、崔景榮並以邊功晉宮保。

translations.literal: Since Heming had repeatedly been impeached, he denounced his impeachers as a faction of villains plotting together, and on the contrary was advanced together with former ministers Huang Jiasheng and Cui Jingrong to Grand Guardian on account of frontier merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heming, impeached repeatedly, called his accusers a cabal of villains—and was promoted to Grand Guardian for frontier merit alongside former ministers Huang Jiasheng and Cui Jingrong.

sentences.zh: 允儀益憤，言：「鶴鳴既以斬級微功邀三次之賞，即當以失地大罪伏不赦之辜。

translations.literal: Yunyi grew even more indignant and said: "Since Heming has claimed three rewards for the slight merit of severed heads, he ought likewise to bear the unpardonable guilt of the great crime of lost territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi's outrage deepened. He wrote: "If Zhang Heming has claimed triple rewards for the paltry merit of counting severed heads, he ought now to answer with the unpardonable crime of losing the frontier.

sentences.zh: 且以七百里之榆關，兼旬而後至，畏縮無丈夫氣，偃蹇無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Moreover, from Yule Pass seven hundred li distant, he arrived only after ten days; he was timid and shrinking, without a man's spirit, arrogant and slothful, without a minister's propriety.
translations.idiomatic: And though Yule Pass lay seven hundred li away, he took ten days to reach it—craven, without the bearing of a man, insolent and lax, without the decorum owed a subject.

sentences.zh: 猶且顏哆口評經、撫功罪，若身在功罪外者。

translations.literal: Yet still with face agape and mouth judging, he appraised the merits and crimes of the military governors and regional commanders, as though he himself stood outside merit and crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still held forth, passing judgment on the governors and commanders as if he stood beyond reward and blame alike.

sentences.zh: 陛下試問鶴鳴，為本兵，功罪殺於邊臣，今日經、撫俱論辟，鶴鳴應得何罪？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, try asking Heming: as Minister of War, merit and guilt were decided by frontier officials; today both military governors and regional commanders are sentenced to execution—what crime should Heming receive?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should ask Zhang Heming: as Minister of War, he let frontier officials decide merit and guilt; now that both governors and commanders face execution, what punishment does he deserve?

sentences.zh: 又問鶴鳴，舊日經、撫俱論辟，嘉善、景榮應得何罪？

translations.literal: Ask Heming again: when formerly military governors and regional commanders were all sentenced to execution, what crimes should Jiasheng and Jingrong receive?
translations.idiomatic: Ask him further: when governors and commanders were condemned to death in the past, what crimes did Huang Jiasheng and Cui Jingrong commit?

sentences.zh: 赫然震怒，論究如法，庶封疆不致破壞。」

translations.literal: Let Your Majesty be manifestly enraged and investigate and punish according to law, so that perhaps the frontier will not be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty thunder in righteous anger and punish them by law—then the frontier may yet be saved."

sentences.zh: 帝不用。

translations.literal: [Close quote] The Emperor did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 會議紅丸事，力詆方從哲，請盡奪官階、祿蔭。

translations.literal: When the Red Pill affair was deliberated, he forcefully denounced Fang Congzhe and requested that all his ranks, stipends, and hereditary privileges be stripped.
translations.idiomatic: During deliberations on the Red Pill affair, he fiercely attacked Fang Congzhe and demanded the complete stripping of his offices, salary, and hereditary privileges.

sentences.zh: 其黨惡之。

translations.literal: His faction hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's faction loathed him for it.

sentences.zh: 徐州舊設參將，山東盜熾，以允儀請，改設總兵。

translations.literal: Xuzhou had formerly had a deputy commander; with banditry raging in Shandong, at Yunyi's request the post was changed to commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou had long had only a deputy commander, but with banditry flaring across Shandong, Yunyi's petition led to the appointment of a full commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋疏論四川監司周著、林宰、徐如珂等功，請優敘。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized on the merits of Sichuan surveillance commissioners Zhou Zhu, Lin Zai, Xu Ruke, and others, requesting preferential recognition.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted a memorial praising the achievements of Sichuan commissioners Zhou Zhu, Lin Zai, Xu Ruke, and others, and asked that they be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 而劾總督張我續退縮，請罷斥。

translations.literal: He also impeached Governor-General Zhang Woxu for shrinking back and requested his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Governor-General Zhang Woxu for cowardice and urged his removal.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The court did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 逾月，請杜傳宣、慎爵賞、免立枷、除苛政。

translations.literal: After a month, he requested an end to palace edicts, careful granting of honors, abolition of standing cangues, and removal of harsh government.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he petitioned to halt palace edicts, curb reckless ennoblement, abolish standing pillories, and end oppressive policies.

sentences.zh: 且言：「向者丁巳之察，凡抗論國本系籍正人者，莫不巧加羅織。

translations.literal: He also said: "In the Dingsi investigation, all upright men who argued against the succession and were registered for it were ingeniously entangled in fabricated charges.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "In the Dingsi purge, every upright official who spoke out on the succession was cunningly framed.

sentences.zh: 陰邪盛而陽氣傷，致有今日之禍。

translations.literal: Yin evil flourished while yang energy was harmed, bringing about today's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Dark intrigue triumphed and righteous force was broken—thus today's disaster.

sentences.zh: 今計期已迫，願當事者早伐邪謀，亟培善類。」

translations.literal: Now the appointed time draws near; I pray those in power will early cut down wicked plots and urgently nurture the good.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis is upon us. I beg those in authority to root out treachery at once and swiftly strengthen the ranks of the upright."

sentences.zh: 疏入，魏忠賢、劉朝輩皆不悅。

translations.literal: [Close quote] When the memorial entered, Wei Zhongxian, Liu Chao, and their ilk were all displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Wei Zhongxian, Liu Chao, and their associates were all displeased.

sentences.zh: 以丁巳主察之人不指名直奏，責令置對。

translations.literal: Because he had not named those who led the Dingsi investigation in a direct memorial, he was ordered to answer for it in person.
translations.idiomatic: Since he had not named the leaders of the Dingsi purge in his memorial, he was ordered to appear and respond.

sentences.zh: 允儀言：「丁巳主察者鄭繼之、李誌也，考功科道則趙士諤、徐紹吉、韓浚也。

translations.literal: Yunyi said: "Those who led the Dingsi investigation were Zheng Jizhi and Li Zhi; the censorate and evaluation officials were Zhao Shie, Xu Shaoji, and Han Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi replied: "The Dingsi investigation was led by Zheng Jizhi and Li Zhi; the censorate and evaluation officials involved were Zhao Shie, Xu Shaoji, and Han Jun.

sentences.zh: 當日八法之處分，臺省之例轉，大僚之拾遺，黑白顛倒，私意橫行。

translations.literal: On that day, the disposition of the eight laws, the transfer of censorate cases, and the picking of oversights among great officials—black and white were inverted and private will ran rampant.
translations.idiomatic: On that day they twisted the eight disciplinary statutes, manipulated censorial procedure, and hunted for pretexts against senior officials—truth and falsehood were reversed and private malice ran unchecked.

sentences.zh: 凡抗論建藩，催請之國，保護先帝，有功國本者，靡不痛加摧抑；

translations.literal: All who argued against establishing a fief, urgently petitioned the throne, protected the late emperor, and served the foundation of the succession—none escaped bitter suppression;
translations.idiomatic: All who had argued against the fief, pressed the succession issue, defended the late emperor, and served the heir's cause were ruthlessly crushed;

sentences.zh: 必欲敗其名，錮其身，盡其倫類而後快。

translations.literal: they had to ruin their names, imprison their persons, and exhaust their kind before they were satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: they would not rest until reputations were ruined, bodies imprisoned, and every ally destroyed.

sentences.zh: 於是方從哲獨居政府，亓詩教、趙興邦等分部要津。

translations.literal: Thus Fang Congzhe alone held the government, while Qi Shijiao, Zhao Xingbang, and others divided the vital passes among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Fang Congzhe dominated the government while Qi Shijiao, Zhao Xingbang, and others seized the key posts.

sentences.zh: 凡疆圉重臣，皆賄賂請托而得，如李維翰、楊鎬、熊廷弼、李如柏、如楨，何一不出其保舉？

translations.literal: All frontier grandees were obtained through bribery and patronage—Li Weihan, Yang Hao, Xiong Tingbi, Li Rubai, and Ruzhen: which of them did not come from their sponsorship?
translations.idiomatic: Every major frontier appointment was bought through bribery and patronage—Li Weihan, Yang Hao, Xiong Tingbi, Li Rubai, Li Ruzhen: not one escaped their recommendation.

sentences.zh: 迨封疆破壞，囹圄充塞，而此輩宴然無恙。

translations.literal: When the frontier was broken and prisons were filled, these men remained secure and unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier collapsed and the prisons overflowed, these men sat untouched at their feasts.

sentences.zh: 臣所以痛心遼事，追恨前此當軸之人也。」

translations.literal: This is why your subject grieves over Liaodong affairs and bitterly regrets those who held power before.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I grieve for Liaodong and bitterly condemn those who once held the reins of power."

sentences.zh: 中旨將重譴允儀，以大學士葉向高言，停俸半歲。

translations.literal: [Close quote] An imperial rescript was about to severely punish Yunyi, but because Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao spoke on his behalf, his salary was suspended for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict was poised to punish Yunyi severely, but Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao interceded, and his salary was suspended for half a year instead.

sentences.zh: 已，復因災祲上言：「內降當停，內操當罷。

translations.literal: Later, again because of calamities and omens he submitted a memorial: "Palace edicts should be halted, and the inner guard corps should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, citing omens and disasters, he memorialized again: "Palace edicts must cease, and the inner guard corps must be disbanded.

sentences.zh: 陵工束手，非所以展孝思；

translations.literal: Imperial tomb works left idle—this is not how filial devotion is shown;
translations.idiomatic: To leave the imperial tombs unfinished is no way to honor filial duty;

sentences.zh: 直臣久廢，非所以光聖德。

translations.literal: upright ministers long discarded—this is not how sagely virtue is displayed.
translations.idiomatic: to keep upright ministers in exile is no way to manifest sage virtue.

sentences.zh: 東南杼柚已空，重以屢次之加派；

translations.literal: The looms of the southeast are already empty, and repeated levies are added on top;
