translations.idiomatic: The looms of the southeast stand empty, yet levy follows levy;

sentences.zh: 金吾冒濫已極，加以非分之襲封。

translations.literal: abuse in the Imperial Guard has reached its limit, and improper enfeoffments are added besides.
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial Guard is bloated with unworthy men, and improper enfeoffments multiply.

sentences.zh: 聖心一轉移，天下無不順應。

translations.literal: If the sacred heart turns but once, nothing under Heaven will fail to respond in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Turn Your Majesty's heart but once, and all under Heaven will follow.

sentences.zh: 區區修禳虛文，安能格上穹哉！」

translations.literal: Mere empty rituals of repair and prayer—how can they move the highest heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Empty rituals of prayer and propitiation will never move Heaven itself!"

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: [Close quote] The Emperor could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，以右僉都御史撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year, he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to pacify and govern Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year, he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent to govern Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 諸府標兵止五百，餉六千，不及一大郡監司。

translations.literal: The standard troops of the prefectures numbered only five hundred, with rations of six thousand—less than a large prefecture's surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures under his charge had only five hundred standard troops and six thousand taels of rations—fewer resources than a single large prefecture's commissioner.

sentences.zh: 且承平久，人不知兵，而屬城率庳薄，無守具。

translations.literal: Moreover, after long peace men did not know war, and subordinate cities were generally low and thin, without defensive equipment.
translations.idiomatic: After decades of peace, no one knew war; the subordinate cities were mostly weak and undefended.

sentences.zh: 六年，流賊將窺湖廣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, roving bandits were about to invade Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, roving rebels threatened to strike Huguang.

sentences.zh: 兵部令移鎮襄陽，鄖陽益虛。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War ordered him to move his headquarters to Xiangyang, leaving Yunyang even more exposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War ordered him to relocate to Xiangyang, leaving Yunyang still more vulnerable.

sentences.zh: 其冬，賊大至，陷鄖西上津。

translations.literal: That winter, bandits arrived in force and took Shangjin in western Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebels came in force and captured Shangjin in western Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 明年，陷房縣、保康。

translations.literal: The next year they took Fang County and Baokang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they seized Fang County and Baokang.

sentences.zh: 允儀兵少，不能禦，上章乞援，且請罪。

translations.literal: Yunyi's troops were few and he could not defend; he submitted a memorial begging for reinforcements and also requesting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi had too few troops to resist; he memorialized for aid and asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 會賊入川，鄖得少緩。

translations.literal: When the bandits entered Sichuan, Yunyang gained a brief respite.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels turned into Sichuan, Yunyang gained a brief reprieve.

sentences.zh: 中官陳大金與左良玉來援，副使徐景麟見其多攜婦女，疑為賊，用炮擊之，士馬多死。

translations.literal: Eunuch Chen Dajin came with Zuo Liangyu to reinforce; Vice Commissioner Xu Jinglin saw that they carried many women and children, suspected them of being bandits, and fired cannon at them, killing many men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Chen Dajin arrived with Zuo Liangyu to reinforce the region; Vice Commissioner Xu Jinglin, seeing their columns crowded with women and children, took them for rebels and opened fire with cannon, killing many men and horses.

sentences.zh: 大金怒，訴諸朝，命逮景麟，責允儀陳狀。

translations.literal: Dajin was enraged and complained to the court; the court ordered Jinglin arrested and commanded Yunyi to submit a report.
translations.idiomatic: Dajin was furious and appealed to the court, which ordered Xu Jinglin arrested and demanded an account from Yunyi.

sentences.zh: 已而並逮允儀下獄，戍邊，而以盧象升代。

translations.literal: Soon Yunyi was also arrested and imprisoned, sentenced to frontier service, and Lu Xiangsheng was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yunyi too was arrested and imprisoned, banished to the frontier, and Lu Xiangsheng replaced him.

sentences.zh: 十五年，御史楊爾銘、給事中倪仁禎相繼論薦，未及用而卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Censor Yang Erming and Supervising Secretary Ni Renzhen successively memorialized recommending him, but before he could be reappointed he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Censor Yang Erming and Supervising Secretary Ni Renzhen successively recommended him for office, but he died before he could be reappointed.

sentences.zh: 鄒維璉，字德輝，江西新昌人。

translations.literal: Zou Weilian, styled Dehui, was a man of Xinchang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Weilian, courtesy name Dehui, was a native of Xinchang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of the Wanli reign he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-fifth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授延平推官。

translations.literal: He was granted appointment as investigating magistrate of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Yanping.

sentences.zh: 耿介有大節。

translations.literal: Upright and unyielding, he possessed great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and resolute, he was a man of unbending principle.

sentences.zh: 巡撫袁一驥以私憾摭布政竇子偁罪，維璉以去就爭。

translations.literal: Governor Yuan Yiji, from private resentment, gathered charges against Administration Commissioner Dou Zicheng; Weilian contested it with threats to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yuan Yiji, nursing a private grudge, fabricated charges against Administration Commissioner Dou Zicheng; Weilian fought the matter to the point of threatening resignation.

sentences.zh: 監司欲為一驥建生祠，維璉抗詞力阻。

translations.literal: The surveillance commissioner wished to build a living shrine for Yiji; Weilian resisted with strong words and forcefully blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: When the surveillance commissioner sought to erect a living shrine to Yuan Yiji, Weilian forcefully opposed it.

sentences.zh: 行取，授南京兵部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: Selected for central appointment, he was made a principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War and promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for service at court, he was appointed principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War and later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 遼左用兵，疏陳數事。

translations.literal: When troops were deployed in Liaodong, he memorialized setting forth several matters.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Liaodong, he submitted a memorial outlining several reforms.

sentences.zh: 尋以憂去。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年，起官職方，進郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Tianqi reign he was raised to the Bureau of Appointments and advanced to director.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Tianqi reign he was recalled to the Bureau of Appointments and promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事譚謙益薦妖人宋明時能役神兵復遼左地，魏忠賢陰主之。

translations.literal: Penal Department principal secretary Tan Qianyi recommended the sorcerer Song Mingshi, who claimed he could command spirit soldiers to recover Liaodong; Wei Zhongxian secretly backed the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Qianyi, a principal secretary in the Penal Department, recommended the sorcerer Song Mingshi, who claimed he could summon spirit armies to recover Liaodong; Wei Zhongxian secretly supported him.

sentences.zh: 維璉極言其妖妄。

translations.literal: Weilian spoke forcefully that it was sorcery and delusion.
translations.idiomatic: Weilian denounced the scheme as rank sorcery and folly.

sentences.zh: 忠賢怒，矯旨譙責。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was enraged and issued a rescript rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was furious and issued an imperial rescript denouncing him.

sentences.zh: 海內方用師，將帥悉賄進，職方尤冗穢。

translations.literal: The realm was then at war, and generals all advanced through bribery; the Bureau of Appointments was especially corrupt and filthy.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was at war, and commanders bought their posts; the Bureau of Appointments was especially rotten.

sentences.zh: 維璉素清嚴，請寄皆絕，因極論債帥之弊，譏切中官、大臣。

translations.literal: Weilian had always been pure and strict; all requests for patronage he refused, and therefore he forcefully argued the evils of debt-ridden generals, satirizing eunuchs and great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Weilian was incorruptible and stern; he rejected every patronage request and launched a fierce attack on the scourge of bought commissions, skewering eunuchs and senior officials alike.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書趙南星知其賢，調為稽勛郎中。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhao Nanxing, knowing his worth, transferred him to be director in the Bureau of Merits.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhao Nanxing, recognizing his talent, transferred him to director in the Bureau of Merits.

sentences.zh: 時言路橫恣，凡用吏部郎，必咨其同鄉居言路者。

translations.literal: At the time the censorial voice ran rampant; whenever a Ministry of Personnel director was appointed, the censor from his home district in the censorial voice had to be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the censorial clique ruled unchecked; every appointment to the Ministry of Personnel required consultation with a censor from the candidate's home province.

sentences.zh: 給事中傅櫆、陳良訓、章允儒以南星不先咨己，大怒，共詬誶維璉。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Fu Zhen, Chen Liangxun, and Zhang Yunru, because Nanxing had not first consulted them, were greatly enraged and together reviled Weilian.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Fu Zhen, Chen Liangxun, and Zhang Yunru, furious that Nanxing had not consulted them first, jointly vilified Weilian.

sentences.zh: 及維璉調考功，櫆等益怒，交章力攻。

translations.literal: When Weilian was transferred to the Bureau of Evaluations, Fu and the others grew angrier still and submitted successive memorials attacking him with full force.
translations.idiomatic: When Weilian was moved to the Bureau of Evaluations, Fu and his allies grew still angrier and launched a barrage of memorials against him.

sentences.zh: 又以江西有吳羽文，例不當用，兩人迫羽文去，以窘辱維璉。

translations.literal: They also cited Wu Yuwen of Jiangxi, who by precedent ought not to be employed; the two men forced Yuwen to leave in order to humiliate Weilian.
translations.idiomatic: They also invoked the case of Wu Yuwen of Jiangxi, who by precedent should not have been appointed; they drove Yuwen out to embarrass Weilian.

sentences.zh: 維璉憤，拜疏求罷，即日出城。

translations.literal: Weilian, in anger, submitted a memorial requesting dismissal and left the city that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Weilian submitted his resignation and left the capital the same day.

sentences.zh: 疏中以章惇攻蘇軾、蔡京逐司馬光為言，櫆等愈怒。

translations.literal: In his memorial he cited Zhang Dun's attack on Su Shi and Cai Jing's expulsion of Sima Guang; Fu and the others grew even angrier.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he invoked Zhang Dun's persecution of Su Shi and Cai Jing's banishment of Sima Guang—Fu and his allies were incensed.

sentences.zh: 櫆遂顯攻魏大中、左光鬥以及維璉。

translations.literal: Fu then openly attacked Wei Dazhong, Zuo Guangdou, and Weilian as well.
translations.idiomatic: Fu then openly attacked Wei Dazhong, Zuo Guangdou, and Weilian.

sentences.zh: 自是朝端水火，諸賢益不安其位矣。

translations.literal: From this the court became fire and water, and worthy men were increasingly unable to rest secure in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the court split into warring camps, and upright officials could no longer hold their posts in peace.

sentences.zh: 維璉欲去不得，詔留視事。

translations.literal: Weilian wished to leave but could not; an edict ordered him to remain and attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: Weilian tried to resign but was refused; an edict ordered him to remain at his post.

sentences.zh: 乃嚴核官評，無少假借。

translations.literal: He then strictly examined official evaluations, granting not the slightest indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: He then conducted official evaluations with unsparing rigor.

sentences.zh: 楊漣劾魏忠賢，被旨切責。

translations.literal: Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian and received an edict sharply rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, the throne answered with a sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 維璉抗疏曰：「忠賢大奸大惡，罄竹難書。

translations.literal: Weilian submitted a defiant memorial saying: "Zhongxian's great treachery and great wickedness—not even bamboo strips could record them all.
translations.idiomatic: Weilian submitted a defiant memorial: "Wei Zhongxian's crimes are so vast that no scroll could contain them all.

sentences.zh: 陛下憐其小信小忠，不忍割棄。

translations.literal: Your Majesty pities his small trustworthiness and small loyalty and cannot bear to cast him off.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty indulges his petty loyalty and petty usefulness and cannot bear to part with him.

sentences.zh: 豈知罪惡既盈，即不忍不可得。

translations.literal: How did you know that once wickedness is full, even unwillingness cannot obtain?
translations.idiomatic: You do not see that when wickedness has run its course, indulgence is no longer possible.

sentences.zh: 漢張讓、趙忠，靈帝以父母稱之；

translations.literal: In Han, Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong—the Spirit Emperor called them father and mother;
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong were called father and mother by Emperor Ling;

sentences.zh: 唐田令孜，僖宗亦以阿父稱之；

translations.literal: In Tang, Tian Lingzi—Emperor Xizong also called him foster father;
translations.idiomatic: in Tang, Tian Lingzi was called foster father by Emperor Xizong;

sentences.zh: 我朝王振、曹吉祥、劉瑾，亦嘗寵之群臣之上。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, Wang Zhen, Cao Jixiang, and Liu Jin were also once favored above all the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: in our dynasty, Wang Zhen, Cao Jixiang, and Liu Jin were once exalted above every minister.

sentences.zh: 有一人老死牖下，獲保富貴哉？

translations.literal: Did even one of them die peacefully at home beneath a window and preserve wealth and honor?
translations.idiomatic: Did any one of them die peacefully in bed, wealth and rank intact?

sentences.zh: 今陛下以太阿授忠賢，非所以為宗社計，亦非所以為忠賢計也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has entrusted the great sword to Zhongxian—this is not planning for the altars of state, nor is it planning for Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has placed the sword of state in Zhongxian's hands—this serves neither the dynasty nor Zhongxian himself.

sentences.zh: 若夫黃扉元老，九列巨卿，安可自處於商輅、劉健、韓文下？」

translations.literal: As for the yellow-door elders and the nine-rank grand ministers, how can they place themselves below Shang Lu, Liu Jian, and Han Wen?
translations.idiomatic: As for the grand secretaries and chief ministers of the nine ministries—can they truly rank themselves below Shang Lu, Liu Jian, and Han Wen?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，責其瀆奏。

translations.literal: [Close quote] When the memorial entered, he was rebuked for irreverent submission.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, he was rebuked for disrespect.

sentences.zh: 崔呈秀坐贓被劾，維璉論戍邊。

translations.literal: When Cui Chengxiu was impeached for corruption, Weilian argued for banishment to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Chengxiu was impeached for embezzlement, Weilian argued that he should be banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 諸媚珰者力別其是非，請托，拒不聽，諸逆黨交憾。

translations.literal: Those who fawned on the eunuchs forcefully disputed right and wrong; they petitioned on his behalf, but he refused to listen, and the faction of traitors jointly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch sycophants contested the verdict; they lobbied him, but he would not yield, and the faction turned against him.

sentences.zh: 及趙南星去國，維璉願與俱去，忠賢即放歸。

translations.literal: When Zhao Nanxing left the capital, Weilian wished to leave with him; Zhongxian immediately released him to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Nanxing left office, Weilian sought to resign with him; Zhongxian promptly allowed him to retire.

sentences.zh: 無何，張訥劾南星，追論維璉調部非法，詔削籍。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhang Na impeached Nanxing and, pursuing the matter, argued that Weilian's transfer to the ministry was illegal; an edict stripped him from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Na impeached Nanxing and, revisiting the case, declared Weilian's transfer to the ministry unlawful; an edict struck him from the register.

sentences.zh: 復構入汪文言獄，下吏，戍貴州。

translations.literal: He was again framed in the Wang Wenyin case, handed to the judicial authorities, and sentenced to frontier service in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then implicated in the Wang Wenyin affair, arrested, and banished to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起南京通政參議，就遷太仆少卿，疏陳卜相、久任、納言、議謚、籌兵五事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was recalled as vice commissioner of the Nanjing Office of Transmission, then promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and memorialized on five matters: selecting ministers, long tenure, receiving remonstrance, deliberating posthumous titles, and planning for troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign he was recalled as vice commissioner of the Nanjing Office of Transmission, then promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, where he memorialized on five reforms: ministerial selection, long tenure, receiving remonstrance, posthumous titles, and military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，擢右僉都御史，代熊文燦巡撫福建。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace Xiong Wencan as governor of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent to replace Xiong Wencan as governor of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 海寇劉香亂，遣遊擊鄭芝龍擊破之。

translations.literal: The sea bandit Liu Xiang rebelled; he dispatched Mobile Corps Commander Zheng Zhilong, who defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirate Liu Xiang rose in rebellion, he dispatched Mobile Corps Commander Zheng Zhilong, who routed him.

sentences.zh: 海外紅夷據彭湖，挾互市，後徙臺灣，漸泊廈門。

translations.literal: Overseas Red Barbarians occupied Penghu, forcing mutual trade; later they moved to Taiwan and gradually anchored at Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Dutch traders held Penghu and demanded trade; they later moved to Taiwan and gradually began anchoring at Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 維璉屢檄芝龍防遏之，不聽。

translations.literal: Weilian repeatedly ordered Zhilong to block them, but he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Weilian repeatedly ordered Zheng Zhilong to intercept them, but Zhilong refused.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，芝龍剿賊福寧，紅夷乘間襲陷廈門城，大掠。

translations.literal: The next summer, as Zhilong was suppressing bandits in Funing, the Red Barbarians seized the opportunity to attack and take Xiamen city, plundering greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer, while Zhilong was suppressing rebels in Funing, the Dutch seized the chance to raid and capture Xiamen, looting the city.

sentences.zh: 維璉急發兵水陸進，芝龍亦馳援，焚其三舟，官軍傷亦眾。

translations.literal: Weilian urgently sent troops by land and water to advance; Zhilong also raced to reinforce, burning three of their ships, though government troops also suffered many casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Weilian urgently dispatched land and naval forces; Zhilong raced to reinforce, and together they burned three enemy ships, though government losses were heavy.

sentences.zh: 寇乃泛舟大洋，轉掠青港、荊嶼、石灣。

translations.literal: The bandits then sailed the open ocean and turned to plunder Qinggang, Jingyu, and Shiwan.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders then put to sea and turned to plunder Qinggang, Jingyu, and Shiwan.

sentences.zh: 諸將禦之銅山，連戰數日，始敗去。

translations.literal: The generals met them at Tongshan; after several days of continuous fighting, they were at last driven off in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Government generals met them at Tongshan; after days of fighting, the raiders were finally driven off.

sentences.zh: 維璉在事二年，勞績甚著。

translations.literal: Weilian was in office two years, and his labor and achievements were very notable.
translations.idiomatic: Weilian served two years in the post, with distinguished results.

sentences.zh: 會當國者溫體仁輩雅忌維璉，而閩人宦京師者騰謗於朝，竟坐是罷官。

translations.literal: As it happened, those holding power such as Wen Tiren always resented Weilian, and Fujianese serving as eunuchs in the capital spread slander at court; he was ultimately dismissed from office on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power, such as Wen Tiren, had long resented Weilian, and Fujianese eunuchs in the capital spread slander at court; on that account he was ultimately dismissed.

sentences.zh: 八年春，敘卻賊功，詔許起用。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year merit was recounted for repelling the bandits, and an edict permitted his recall.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year, when merit for repelling the bandits was reviewed, an edict permitted his recall to office.

sentences.zh: 旋召拜兵部右侍郎，遘疾不赴，卒於家。

translations.literal: He was soon summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of War, but encountered illness and did not go; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as right vice minister of war, but fell ill and could not take up the post; he died at home.

sentences.zh: 吳羽文既謝病歸，至崇禎六年始復出。

translations.literal: After Wu Yuwen had resigned on account of illness and returned home, he did not emerge again until the sixth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Yuwen resigned on account of illness and returned home, he did not reenter office until the sixth year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 歷考功文選郎中。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of Director in the Bureau of Evaluations and the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as director in the Bureau of Evaluations and the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 帝以積疑吏部有私，選郎十一人譴黜大半，遷者三人而已。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of long-standing suspicion that the Ministry of Personnel showed favoritism, censured and dismissed most of the eleven selection secretaries; only three were transferred.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having long suspected the Ministry of Personnel of favoritism, censured and dismissed most of the eleven selection secretaries, transferring only three.

sentences.zh: 羽文痛絕諸弊，數與溫體仁牴牾。

translations.literal: Yuwen deeply hated all abuses and repeatedly clashed with Wen Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen loathed official abuses and repeatedly clashed with Wen Tiren.

sentences.zh: 賕毀皇陵，有詔肆赦。

translations.literal: Bribery damaged the imperial tombs, and there was an edict granting a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Bribery had damaged the imperial tombs, and an edict proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 體仁令刑部尚書馮英以逆案入詔內。

translations.literal: Tiren ordered Minister of Punishments Feng Ying to insert treason cases into the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren ordered Minister of Punishments Feng Ying to insert treason cases into the amnesty edict.

sentences.zh: 羽文執止之，而議起錢龍錫、李邦華等。

translations.literal: Yuwen held firm and stopped it, yet debate arose over Qian Longxi, Li Banghua, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen held firm and stopped it, yet debate arose over whether to include Qian Longxi, Li Banghua, and others.

sentences.zh: 偵事者誣羽文納二人賊，下獄。

translations.literal: Spies slandered Yuwen for taking bribes from the two men and he was sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Spies accused Yuwen of taking bribes from the two men, and he was sent to prison.

sentences.zh: 羽文用高鳳翔為大名知府。

translations.literal: Yuwen employed Gao Fengxiang as prefect of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen appointed Gao Fengxiang prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔故嘗坐小罰，言者復謂其徇私，坐謫戍。

translations.literal: Fengxiang had formerly received a minor punishment; remonstrators again said he showed private favor and he was sentenced to demotion and frontier guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang had once received a minor punishment; critics again charged favoritism, and Yuwen was sentenced to demotion and frontier guard duty.

sentences.zh: 侍郎吳甡等交薦，復官，未赴卒。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wu Shen and others jointly recommended him; his office was restored, but before he could go he died.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wu Shen and others jointly recommended him; his office was restored, but he died before he could take it up.

sentences.zh: 羽文，字長卿，南昌人。

translations.literal: Yuwen, style name Changqing, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen, whose style was Changqing, came from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：王汝訓諸人建言，挺謇諤之節，洊歷卿貳，不隕厥問。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Wang Ruxun and the others in remonstrating upheld the integrity of outspoken integrity; promoted repeatedly to ministerial rank, they did not lose their reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Wang Ruxun and his colleagues, in their remonstrances, upheld the integrity of blunt speech; promoted repeatedly to high office, they did not lose their standing.

sentences.zh: 余懋學之言十蠹，有以哉！

translations.literal: Yu Maoxue's words on the ten corruptions—there was reason in them!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Maoxue's words on the ten corruptions—how well founded they were!

sentences.zh: 鄒維璉抗魏奄，拒逆黨，僅坐謫戍，幸矣。

translations.literal: Zou Weilian resisted the Wei eunuch, rejected the treacherous faction, and received only demotion to frontier guard duty—he was fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Weilian resisted Wei Zhongxian, rejected the treacherous faction, and received only banishment to frontier guard duty—he was fortunate indeed.
